Hi Dana,

Good morning — I hope you’re doing well.


I’m reaching out regarding the Bodybar permit application currently under review (SIGN-2026-00119), specifically in response to the review comment requesting confirmation that the application is for window signs only (see below).


To clarify, the intent of this submittal is indeed for window graphics only.


We had previously submitted a separate application for the wall signage (SIGN-2026-00088), which has already gone through review and corrections. 

Rather than modifying that application further, we proceeded with a separate submittal for the window graphics to keep the scopes distinct.


That said, I wanted to check with you to confirm whether this is the preferred approach, or if you would recommend combining the window graphics scope into the existing application (SIGN-2026-00088) instead.


We’re happy to proceed in whichever manner aligns best with your review process.


Thank you for your guidance, and please let me know how you’d like us to proceed.


Best regards,

subject: Town of Gilbert -  SIGN-2026-00088 Your Permit is Now Available
body:
Your approved permit is attached. Visit our OneStopShop <https://onestopshop.gilbertaz.gov/>  portal to download any approved plans. These can be viewed under the “attachments” section of your permit. Approved plans and permit must be printed and available at the time of your inspections. 

To print a copy of your permit, please use the printer icon in OneStopShop to print your permit. If you do not see the printer icon and your permit is in an "Issued" status, please contact us at EplanBuilding@gilbertaz.gov. 

A one-time registration is required. If you have not already registered, please use this link <https://onestopshop.gilbertaz.gov/>  to do so. Please allow one business day following your registration to gain full access to the OneStopShop portal. 

You will also be able to request inspections as well as monitor inspection results. The OneStopShop is also available for online payments and to apply for future permits. 

For any questions, please call our Development Services team (480) 503-6700, Mon-Thurs 7am-6pm. Offices are closed Fridays and Holidays. 

Thank you, 

Town of Gilbert
Development Services
Ph: 480-503-6700

*We are transitioning online applications from our current ePlan Review to OneStopShop. OneStopShop online applications are currently limited to select permit types: Commercial and Residential Trade permits, Swimming pools, Engineering Utility Permits, Deferred Submittals and Plan Changes. All others must be applied for through our ePlan Review <http://general.gilbertaz.gov/eforms/eplan/BLDGSubmits/ePlanAppConst.cfm>  process.

subject: Town of Gilbert SIGN-2026-00088 Sign permit issued
body:
Dear Customer, 

Thank you for obtaining your permit for your signage here in Gilbert. Please be aware you will need to schedule and complete all applicable inspections relating to this permit. Approved plans must be on-site at the time of your inspection. Please login to our OneStopShop <https://onestopshop.gilbertaz.gov/>  to print your approved plans, pay fees and schedule all inspections. Approved plans can be viewed/printed under the “attachments” section of your permit. 

At this time your scheduled inspection may be eligible for either an onsite or virtual inspection*. The area inspector will contact you if your inspection is eligible to be conducted virtually, otherwise your onsite inspection will be completed as scheduled.

Approved plans and permit must be printed and available at the time of your inspection(s).

For any questions, please call our Development Services team (480) 503-6700, Mon-Thurs 7am-6pm. Offices are closed Fridays and Holidays.

Thank you, 
Town of Gilbert
Development Services
Ph: 480-503-6700 

*For Virtual Inspections, you will need to have the following items:
1.) Measuring tape
2.) Copy of permit application and plans indicating proper distancing and location of sign 
3.) Phone availability of either Facetime, Zoom, Teams or another software program that will allow face to face interaction with the inspector.

Hi Wendy,

We have recently received three separate emails from the City of Avondale (Linda Hearing, Sign Department) regarding outstanding sign permit applications that require attention.


After reviewing the portal (see attached screenshot ), it appears we currently have a mix of application statuses that need to be cleaned up and brought to closure. These generally fall into three categories:

• Ready for Issuance / Fees Due – Applications that are approved but pending payment
• Issued / Pending Final – Permits that now require inspection scheduling and close-out
• Inactive / No Longer Needed – Applications that may need to be formally withdrawn or cancelled


Now, these are sitting in various stages without a coordinated push to completion, which is what prompted the City’s follow-up.


Additionally, this is not isolated to Avondale — we are seeing similar situations across other jurisdictions where permits are either awaiting fees, inspections, or finalization. This would be a good opportunity to treat this as a focused cleanup effort across the board to:

• Clear out outstanding fees
• Schedule and complete required inspections
• Close out or cancel any inactive permits
• Bring all records to a finalized state


This is not urgent in the immediate sense, but it does require dedicated attention to prevent ongoing follow-ups from jurisdictions and to keep our records current and clean.


Let me know when you’d like to prioritize this, and I can begin organizing a structured list and action plan to work through everything efficiently.

Subject: Avondale Sign Permit Applications – Status Cleanup Needed (04/15/26) 
 

Hi Wendy,



We have recently received three separate emails from the City of Avondale (Linda Hearing, Sign Department) regarding outstanding sign permit applications that require attention.


After reviewing the portal (see attached screenshot ), it appears we currently have a mix of application statuses that need to be cleaned up and brought to closure. These generally fall into three categories:



• Ready for Issuance / Fees Due – Applications that are approved but pending payment
• Issued / Pending Final – Permits that now require inspection scheduling and close-out
• Inactive / No Longer Needed – Applications that may need to be formally withdrawn or cancelled


Now, these are sitting in various stages without a coordinated push to completion, which is what prompted the City’s follow-up.


Additionally, this is not isolated to Avondale — we are seeing similar situations across other jurisdictions where permits are either awaiting fees, inspections, or finalization. This would be a good opportunity to treat this as a focused cleanup effort across the board to:

• Clear out outstanding fees
• Schedule and complete required inspections
• Close out or cancel any inactive permits
• Bring all records to a finalized state


This is not urgent in the immediate sense, but it does require dedicated attention to prevent ongoing follow-ups from jurisdictions and to keep our records current and clean.


Let me know when you’d like to prioritize this, and I can begin organizing a structured list and action plan to work through everything efficiently.


Best regards,

subject: Town of Gilbert -  SIGN-2026-00019 Your Permit is Now Available
body:
Your approved permit is attached. Visit our OneStopShop <https://onestopshop.gilbertaz.gov/>  portal to download any approved plans. These can be viewed under the “attachments” section of your permit. Approved plans and permit must be printed and available at the time of your inspections. 

To print a copy of your permit, please use the printer icon in OneStopShop to print your permit. If you do not see the printer icon and your permit is in an "Issued" status, please contact us at EplanBuilding@gilbertaz.gov. 

A one-time registration is required. If you have not already registered, please use this link <https://onestopshop.gilbertaz.gov/>  to do so. Please allow one business day following your registration to gain full access to the OneStopShop portal. 

You will also be able to request inspections as well as monitor inspection results. The OneStopShop is also available for online payments and to apply for future permits. 

For any questions, please call our Development Services team (480) 503-6700, Mon-Thurs 7am-6pm. Offices are closed Fridays and Holidays. 

Thank you, 

Town of Gilbert
Development Services
Ph: 480-503-6700

*We are transitioning online applications from our current ePlan Review to OneStopShop. OneStopShop online applications are currently limited to select permit types: Commercial and Residential Trade permits, Swimming pools, Engineering Utility Permits, Deferred Submittals and Plan Changes. All others must be applied for through our ePlan Review <http://general.gilbertaz.gov/eforms/eplan/BLDGSubmits/ePlanAppConst.cfm>  process.

subject: Town of Gilbert SIGN-2026-00019 Sign permit issued
body:
Dear Customer, 

Thank you for obtaining your permit for your signage here in Gilbert. Please be aware you will need to schedule and complete all applicable inspections relating to this permit. Approved plans must be on-site at the time of your inspection. Please login to our OneStopShop <https://onestopshop.gilbertaz.gov/>  to print your approved plans, pay fees and schedule all inspections. Approved plans can be viewed/printed under the “attachments” section of your permit. 

At this time your scheduled inspection may be eligible for either an onsite or virtual inspection*. The area inspector will contact you if your inspection is eligible to be conducted virtually, otherwise your onsite inspection will be completed as scheduled.

Approved plans and permit must be printed and available at the time of your inspection(s).

For any questions, please call our Development Services team (480) 503-6700, Mon-Thurs 7am-6pm. Offices are closed Fridays and Holidays.

Thank you, 
Town of Gilbert
Development Services
Ph: 480-503-6700 

*For Virtual Inspections, you will need to have the following items:
1.) Measuring tape
2.) Copy of permit application and plans indicating proper distancing and location of sign 
3.) Phone availability of either Facetime, Zoom, Teams or another software program that will allow face to face interaction with the inspector.

Attached is a photo of the southwest elevation (taken during the original sign installation). Based on this, we think it may be worth considering placing the display in that location.


Given the building conditions and available wall space, a wall-mounted sign would likely be the stronger solution here. This elevation provides a clean, visible surface that would allow us to:

• Simplify structural and permitting requirements
• Create a more cohesive look with the building façade
• Avoid limitations tied to the existing bracket system


If you’re open to it, we can put together a few wall sign concepts that carry that classic DiMaggio’s identity—incorporating the vintage/neon feel we discussed—just applied in a way that better fits the architecture.

                Here is side by side by side.  

 

The 8’ tall sign is the max height of ground sign the lot can have per code.  

 

Then you must follow all the required setbacks needed in between the back of sidewalk & multi use trail and see if that 8’ tall sign will fit for placement.  It does not fit per code at all in that space & per city email was not recommended to place any sign there and to go behind the trail.

 

Need 5’ setback from back side of sidewalk and min. 3’ away from front of trail.  8’ of setbacks.   If we have 12’ in between these two points for sure.   Then sign max width can be 4’ max.  See pdf for that one.

 

FYI - This is if indeed there is 12’ wide area between back side of sidewalk and front side of trail And you clear all the in ground utilities in that exact spot (see below from GC) & you get city to accept new landscaping plan to move a few items from that exact spot for the new smaller monument location and find new spots on lot to replace those plants & Maybe have to re-submit new landscape plan to city for review and approval (TBD by Others) & that those other plants that stay all along the front that would be around the shorter sign don’t over grow and block it (See photo below).

 

If you only have 11’ of space, then after setbacks we can do about a 3’ max wide sign.  See pdf for that one.

body:
Ticket Status Notification

Ticket Information

Ticket Number: 2026040801216

Ticket Location: N VERRADO WAY
BUCKEYE, MARICOPA, AZ United States
33.4568939106352, -112.503457639048 

Due Date: 04/10/2026 8:00 PM ET

Company: CHRISTY SIGNS

Phone: 6022424488

Fax/Email:  / STEVE@CHRISTYSIGNS.COM

 




Reason for Notification

Notification Type: Bore Standby        Date: 04/08/2026

You have indicated on the Locate Request(s) that you intend to use Boring in your work area. To ensure the integrity of our system, Southwest Gas is requesting you call us prior to exposing our facilities. Southwest Gas requires a representative to be present to verify our facilities prior to boring across or parallel within 5-feet of Southwest Gas facilities. This is to confirm that you have in fact exposed our line and confirm the line depth to assure a safe bore operation by positive identification of our facilities. Call to schedule a standby a minimum of two hours prior to work identified above.

Notify an SWG representative when boring parallel to any Southwest Gas facilities within 5-feet of the bore. This applies to vertical boring as well.

1.	Notify an SWG representative when boring across any Southwest Gas facilities.

2.	Pothole any gas facilities within 24-inches of the proposed bore path.

3.	Hand digging is required within 24-inches of the gas facility markings, and all gas facilities must be identified, protected, and exposed during any boring operations.

4.	Before the excavation, schedule a Bore Standby with a SWG representative to be present to verify the buried facilities and monitor the boring activities.

Please contact your local SWG field office to schedule a Bore Standby with a Southwest Gas representative a

minimum of 2 hours prior.

 602-484-5086

 For more information regarding safe digging practices, please visit swgas.com

Locate Requester will notify its employees and any of their subcontractors of these requirements.

If you have any questions or need any assistance, please notify Southwest Gas immediately.

Southwest Gas Corporation Business Hours (Mon-Fri between 600 a.m. & 2:30 p.m.) After Hours Emergency: 877-860-6020

EXCAVATOR PRECAUTIONARY GUIDELINES

 

This information is to assist excavators in the proper identification of gas facilities, and precautions to be taken when working around gas facilities.  The information provided here is not to be considered all-inclusive. All excavators digging within the vicinity of gas pipelines must protect the pipelines in accordance with the applicable One-Call law. The following are guidelines that will assist you in protecting the public, you, and the gas facilities.

If any gas pipelines are damaged, federal law requires that you call Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Additionally, if the damage results in the escape of gas, you must call the Emergency Number 911.  Note: Damage includes damage to steel pipeline coatings, gouges in plastic pipe, damaged tracer wire, dents or scrapes in steel pipe, etc.

Gas pipeline markers are used to alert the public that gas pipelines are buried in the general area. These markers may or may not be placed directly over the gas facility. When performing an excavation within 10’ of a “High Pressure” marked facility, please contact SWG to arrange for stand by personnel to be present.

 

PLASTIC PIPELINES:  Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) pipe is one type of plastic pipe used in the SWG gas distribution system.  PVC may be faint yellow, gray or white in color and range in size from ½" to 2" in diameter.  PVC is not as flexible as the polyethylene (PE) pipe that SWG installs today. The integrity of PVC can be compromised if scratched or subjected to external loads and/or stresses.  PE is another type of plastic pipe used in SWG’s system.  PE may be found in various colors and range in size from ½" to 8" in diameter.  Although PE is a more flexible material, its integrity can be compromised if scratched or nicked.  Many plastic gas pipelines are installed with a tracer wire in order to locate the facility.  If a tracer wire is or has been severed or damaged, call SWG.  We will repair the damaged wire at no charge.

 

STEEL PIPELINES: Steel gas pipelines, used in both SWG gas distribution and high-pressure transmission systems, range in size from ½" to 24" in diameter and are also susceptible to damage.  Dents and gouges in the steel will affect the integrity of the pipe, so precautionary measures must be taken during excavation.  Steel pipelines are protected with an approved coating material that helps prevent deterioration of the pipe and can be found in various colors.  If during excavation the coating is torn or damaged, contact SWG immediately to facilitate the repairs at no charge.  Call us before disturbing any mastic coating on active or abandoned steel pipe.  The coating is likely to contain regulated asbestos fibers that can be harmful to your employees.

 

Typically, most gas pipes have specific identification markings on them or on the coating.  Care should be taken to support and protect all gas pipelines, as required by law, when exposed or crossed during excavation activities.  Additionally, care must be taken while exposing existing facilities as they may or may not have padding and shading surrounding them as outlined below.  If any gas pipeline is damaged, call SWG immediately to facilitate the proper pipeline repairs.  When excavations have been completed, gas pipelines must be properly padded, shaded, and backfilled per SWG standards, as shown in the drawing below.  SWG specifications for padding and shading material call for it to be able to sift through a 3/8" screen and be smooth and relatively rock free.  Excavations must be compacted to meet the requirements of local authorities.  During backfill activities it is very important to compact the soil beneath the gas pipe to properly support it. Also, it is important to avoid mechanically compacting the soil directly over the gas pipe to eliminate any unnecessary external stresses.  Steps must be taken during this process to protect the gas pipeline from excessive external loadings.  If other utilities or substructures are to be installed in the same excavation as a gas pipeline, the proper clearances shown in the drawing must be maintained.

If at any time during excavation activities you smell gas, call SWG and 911.

*	DO NOT attempt to control or stop the flow of natural gas, or make repairs.
*	DO NOT turn on, turn off, or attempt to move or operate equipment near the line break or point of leakage.
*	DO NOT enter the area where the natural gas is escaping.
*	DO NOT allow others to enter the area.
*	DO NOT leave the scene of the incident until assistance has arrived.
*	DO secure the area and prevent others from entering.
*	DO eliminate sources of ignition, such as sparks or flames, near the gaseous atmosphere.

For more information on the types of gas pipe used by SWG, positive identification of gas facilities, or if you have any questions, please contact the SWG office nearest you. Additional information on natural gas safety is included in our Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) located at www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .

Please forward to the appropriate excavator.




Esta información tiene como objetivo ayudar a los excavadores a identificar adecuadamente las instalaciones de gas y a conocer las precauciones que deben tener cuando trabajan cerca de ellas. La información aquí provista no es exhaustiva. Todos los excavadores que trabajen en cercanías de gasoductos deben protegerlos de acuerdo con la ley vigente sobre excavaciones. Las siguientes son pautas que lo ayudarán a proteger al público, a usted mismo y a las instalaciones de gas.

Si el gasoducto está dañado, la ley federal exige que llame a Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Además, si el daño causa un escape de gas, debe llamar al número para emergencias 911. Nota: Los daños pueden ser daños en el recubrimiento de las tuberías de acero, aberturas en las tuberías plásticas, daños en el alambre de rastreo, mellas o raspaduras en las tuberías de acero, etc.

 

Se usan señales para advertir al público de que hay gasoductos enterrados en el área. Estas señales pueden ponerse directamente sobre la instalación de gas o no. Cuando se lleva a cabo una excavación dentro de los 10’ de una instalación señalizada como “High Pressure” (de alta presión), comuníquese con SWG para que envíen personal de respaldo.

TUBERÍAS PLÁSTICAS Las tuberías de policloruro de vinilo (PVC) son un tipo de tubería plástica que SWG usa en el sistema de distribución. Las tuberías de PVC pueden ser de color amarillo claro, gris o blanco, y su tamaño puede ir desde ½” hasta 2” de diámetro. Las tuberías de PVC no son tan flexibles como las de polietileno (PE) que SWG instala hoy. El PVC puede arruinarse si se raya o se somete a pesos o tensiones extremos. Las tuberías de PE son otro tipo de tuberías plásticas que SWG usa en su sistema. Las tuberías de PE pueden ser de varios colores, y su tamaño va desde ½” hasta 8” de diámetro. Aunque el PE es un material más flexible, puede arruinarse si se raya o corta. Muchos gasoductos de plástico se instalan con un alambre de rastreo para ubicar la instalación. Si el alambre de rastreo se corta o daña, llame a SWG. Lo repararemos sin cargo.

 

TUBERÍAS DE ACERO Las tuberías de gas de acero, usadas por SWG tanto para la distribución de gas como para los sistemas de transmisión a alta presión, varían en tamaño desde 1/2" hasta 24" de diámetro y también son susceptibles a los daños. Las mellas y aberturas en el acero pueden afectar la integridad de la tubería. Por eso, deben tomarse medidas de precaución durante la excavación. Las tuberías de acero se protegen con un material de recubrimiento aprobado que ayuda a prevenir su deterioro y puede ser de varios colores. Si durante la excavación el recubrimiento se desprende o daña, comuníquese con SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones sin cargo. Llámenos antes de quitar cualquier recubrimiento de masilla de una tubería de acero activa o abandonada. Es posible que el recubrimiento contenga fibras de amianto reglamentario que pueden ser dañinas para sus empleados.

 

En general, las tuberías de gas tienen marcas de identificación específicas sobre ellas o sobre el recubrimiento. Debe tenerse precaución y sostener y proteger todos los gasoductos, según lo requiera la ley, cuando se expongan o crucen durante la excavación. Además, debe tenerse cuidado al exponer instalaciones existentes, ya que pueden o no, tener relleno a su alrededor, como se detalla más abajo. Si un gasoducto está dañado, llame a SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones necesarias. Cuando finalicen las excavaciones, los gasoductos deben ser rellenados según las normas de SWG, como se muestra en el dibujo más abajo. Las especificaciones de SWG para el material de relleno indican que este debe poder pasar a través de un tamiz de 3/8”, ser suave y estar relativamente libre de escombros.  Las excavaciones deben ser compactadas para cumplir con los requisitos de las autoridades locales. Durante el rellenado, es muy importante compactar el suelo bajo el gasoducto, a fin de sujetarlo apropiadamente. También es importante evitar compactar mecánicamente el suelo que está sobre el gasoducto para eliminar tensiones externas innecesarias. Deben tomarse medidas durante este proceso para proteger el gasoducto de cargas externas excesivas. Si se deben instalar otros servicios o subestructuras en la misma excavación del gasoducto, deben respetarse las distancias que se muestran en el dibujo.

Si en cualquier momento durante la excavación percibe olor a gas, llame a SWG y al 911.

*	NO intente controlar ni parar el flujo de gas natural ni de hacer reparaciones.
*	NO encienda, apague ni intente mover u operar equipos cerca del punto donde se rompió la línea o se produjo el escape.
*	NO entre en un área donde haya un escape de gas natural.
*	NO permita que otras personas entren en dicha área.
*	NO deje el lugar del incidente hasta que llegue la ayuda.
*	DESPEJE el área y evite que otras personas entren en ella.
*	ELIMINE las fuentes de combustión, como chispas o llamas, cerca de la atmósfera gaseosa.

Si desea más información sobre los tipos de tuberías de gas usados por SWG o sobre cómo identificar instalaciones de gas, o si tiene preguntas, llame a la oficina de SWG más cercana. En nuestra hoja de datos de seguridad de material (MSDS), puede encontrar más información sobre la seguridad con el gas natural. Esta se encuentra en www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .






Favor de hacer llegar al excavador correspondiente.

subject: Town of Gilbert -  SIGN-2026-00055 Your Permit is Now Available
body:
Your approved permit is attached. Visit our OneStopShop <https://onestopshop.gilbertaz.gov/>  portal to download any approved plans. These can be viewed under the “attachments” section of your permit. Approved plans and permit must be printed and available at the time of your inspections. 

To print a copy of your permit, please use the printer icon in OneStopShop to print your permit. If you do not see the printer icon and your permit is in an "Issued" status, please contact us at EplanBuilding@gilbertaz.gov. 

A one-time registration is required. If you have not already registered, please use this link <https://onestopshop.gilbertaz.gov/>  to do so. Please allow one business day following your registration to gain full access to the OneStopShop portal. 

You will also be able to request inspections as well as monitor inspection results. The OneStopShop is also available for online payments and to apply for future permits. 

For any questions, please call our Development Services team (480) 503-6700, Mon-Thurs 7am-6pm. Offices are closed Fridays and Holidays. 

Thank you, 

Town of Gilbert
Development Services
Ph: 480-503-6700

*We are transitioning online applications from our current ePlan Review to OneStopShop. OneStopShop online applications are currently limited to select permit types: Commercial and Residential Trade permits, Swimming pools, Engineering Utility Permits, Deferred Submittals and Plan Changes. All others must be applied for through our ePlan Review <http://general.gilbertaz.gov/eforms/eplan/BLDGSubmits/ePlanAppConst.cfm>  process.

subject: Town of Gilbert SIGN-2026-00055 Sign permit issued
body:
Dear Customer, 

Thank you for obtaining your permit for your signage here in Gilbert. Please be aware you will need to schedule and complete all applicable inspections relating to this permit. Approved plans must be on-site at the time of your inspection. Please login to our OneStopShop <https://onestopshop.gilbertaz.gov/>  to print your approved plans, pay fees and schedule all inspections. Approved plans can be viewed/printed under the “attachments” section of your permit. 

At this time your scheduled inspection may be eligible for either an onsite or virtual inspection*. The area inspector will contact you if your inspection is eligible to be conducted virtually, otherwise your onsite inspection will be completed as scheduled.

Approved plans and permit must be printed and available at the time of your inspection(s).

For any questions, please call our Development Services team (480) 503-6700, Mon-Thurs 7am-6pm. Offices are closed Fridays and Holidays.

Thank you, 
Town of Gilbert
Development Services
Ph: 480-503-6700 

*For Virtual Inspections, you will need to have the following items:
1.) Measuring tape
2.) Copy of permit application and plans indicating proper distancing and location of sign 
3.) Phone availability of either Facetime, Zoom, Teams or another software program that will allow face to face interaction with the inspector.

subject: RE: Jas Diesel – Sign Permit Follow-Up (LPSG 251389) (04/02/26)
body:
Thank you for the information, Steve

 

It looks like this price panel is being used in the correct manner, but its technology is comparable to the electronic message display utilized on the same sign. For this reason, I cannot move this project forward.

Some insight to my conclusion - All EMD’s are required to submit for use permit approval, this was not always the case. If a customer decided the display would be “static” they could circumvent this process. Obviously, this did not work out as expected and a change needed to be made. The intended use of the display does not handicap it’s features.

 

I’ll need to see schematics that show this price panel is anything but an additional full color display unit.

 

Thank you,

Hi Jacob, Thank you for your review and for raising this concern. We understand the question regarding the display’s ability to present content beyond fuel pricing. The attached Fuel Price Display Narrative outlines the intended use and operational

Hi Jacob,

Thank you for your review and for raising this concern.


We understand the question regarding the display’s ability to present content beyond fuel pricing. The attached Fuel Price Display Narrative outlines the intended use and operational framework of the fuel price panels.


In practice, when operated in a static setting, the display functions the same as a fuel price changer, presenting fixed pricing rather than variable messaging.


In the same manner that the City’s Use Permit establishes how the display must be operated—including automatic shutoff at 10:00 PM, display timing requirements, and brightness limits not to exceed 300 nits—the static fuel price display is achieved through system configuration and operation.


We have also included Cirrus documentation demonstrating that the display system can maintain a fixed image, control brightness, and implement scheduled operation to meet these requirements.


The fuel price panels operate within this same compliance-based framework and are used to display fuel pricing only.


Please let me know if you would like any additional detail or to review the system configuration further.


Best regards,

Steve Skye

Jacob,

Thank you for your review and detailed feedback.


We would like to provide clarification regarding the EMD square footage calculation noted in the corrections.


Per the approved Use Permit stipulations, the maximum electronic message display (EMD) area is limited to 40 square feet . Our understanding and intent is that this requirement applies specifically to the programmable message display portion of the sign.


The current design includes:

*	40 square feet of electronic message display (EMD) used for changeable messaging 
*	20 square feet of fuel price displays, which are static price changers 


The fuel price components:

*	Are not used for messaging or advertising 
*	Do not function as an electronic message center 
*	Are regulated separately, as fuel pricing is required to be continuously and accurately displayed for operational compliance 


Because of this distinction, the fuel price displays should not be considered part of the EMD area calculation. The EMD portion of the sign remains compliant with the 40 square foot limitation as outlined in the Use Permit.


Additionally, we note that the prior approval did not include stipulations restricting the configuration in this manner , further supporting the interpretation that the EMD limitation applies specifically to the message display portion.


We would appreciate your confirmation on this interpretation so we may proceed accordingly without unnecessary redesign.


Thank you,

subject: Retrofit an Existing Sign with an EMC in Under an Hour
body:
Hi Steve,







 




Cirrus LED will be exhibiting at ISA Sign Expo 2026, and we’d love to connect with you at Booth 541.

One of the new products we’ll be showcasing is our patent-pending retrofit display cabinet.




This is designed specifically for retrofitting an existing static sign with a new EMC. What used to take 5–6 hours on site, can now be done in under an hour. This lightweight aluminum cabinet is ready to bolt on with no welding, no fabrication, and no specialized tools required.




It’s a major unlock for our sign shop partners—lightning fast installs, lower labor costs, and the ability to turn more static signs into digital revenue drivers.




We’ll have it on site at Booth 541 so you can see exactly how it works.




Best regards,

		• Electrical certification confirming that the display does not exceed 300 nits brightness

On Tue, Mar 31, 2026 at 3:23 PM Steve Skye <steve@christysigns.com <mailto:steve@christysigns.com> > wrote:


	Hi Rebekah,
	
	

	Thank you again for taking the time to speak with me earlier today — I appreciate it.

	
	I wanted to follow up regarding the Jas Diesel project. We are currently working through plan review comments with the city, and one of the key items relates to the fuel price display portion of the sign.

	
	The reviewer’s concern is tied to the drawings identifying both the message display and fuel price panels similarly, and specifically noted:

	“The ability to display something other than the price of fuel is what I am concerned with.”

	
	To address this, we have prepared a narrative (attached) clarifying that the fuel price panels are used strictly for fuel pricing in accordance with Arizona regulatory requirements, and that the system is operated in a manner consistent with static price displays.

	
	To help support this with the city, we are looking to provide a bit more clarity from the manufacturer side. Would you be able to assist with the following:

	• A brief description or statement confirming that the display system can be operated to present fixed (non-changing) content, such as fuel pricing
	• Any guidance or documentation on how this type of use is typically configured or managed within the system

	
	Additionally, the city has requested the following:

	• Electrical certification confirming that the display does not exceed 300 nits brightness

	
	If Cirrus has a standard specification sheet, certification, or statement addressing brightness levels (or the ability to limit brightness), that would be very helpful for our submittal.

	
	The goal here is simply to provide clarity on how the system is used in practice so the city can feel comfortable with the distinction and move the permit forward.

	
	Thanks again for your help on this — I appreciate your support.

	
	Best regards,
	
	

	Steve Skye

subject: SGN26-06 -- U-Haul Maricopa
body:
Hi Steve,

Thank you for submitting a sign permit application for U-Haul Maricopa. After initially reviewing the application, I noticed that multiple signs are proposed per elevation and the aggregate sign area exceeds 100 sq. ft., which conflicts with the city's sign code (Section 18.115 <https://maricopa.municipal.codes/MCC/18.115> ). If you would like to remain with the proposed signage, our code allows for a comprehensive sign plan to create specific sign standards for the U-Haul site. The cost would be $1,111.00 and staff review is usually 2-3 weeks per review.

The submittal requirements for a CSP are as follows:

1.	
	CSP Booklet: site location, site plan, sign inventory and exhibits, deviations from the zoning code, etc. 
2.	
	Owner Authorization Letter: a letter from the property owner or authorized representative allowing the CSP.


Let me know how you would like to proceed with this proposal. Feel free to reach out with any questions.

Thank you,

The card keeps moving counterclockwise 🔄 If the card comes back to the original player in the SAME round: ✅ They may keep the card * But must discard one of their other 2 cards into the middle of the discard pile ________________________________ 😎 “GOTCHA!” MOVE * If the player on your left has a 6 or 7: * You may give them a card instead of discarding * Only do this if it will make them lose their 6 or 7 ________________________________ 🏆 HOW TO WIN * Get both the 6 and the 7 * Keep them until the end of your turn * If you don’t lose them… you win! 🎉 ________________________________ 💡 TIP Try not to hold cards that can combine to make your 6 or 7! ________________________________ 💌 Layout Suggestions for Printing: * Use bold headings and colored borders for each section * Add emoji icons next to section titles for fun visual cues * Use tables or card placeholders for players to mark their hands if desired * Include a small example math box to remind players of the 6–7 rule ________________________________ If you want, I can actually mock up a visually styled one-page sheet with boxes, borders, and playful fonts so it’s ready to print and looks like a real game sheet. Do you want me to create that mockup next? show me the mock up just like you have it but with the bold headings and colorful borders. keep the emoji icons you have now Perfect! I’ve created a mockup of your 6/7 Card Game sheet with bold headings, colored borders, and the emoji icons intact. You can copy this into Word, Google Docs, Canva, or any editor for printing. I’ve used color names in brackets so you can apply them in your editor. ________________________________
🎴 6/7 CARD GAME Ages: 6–70 | Players: 2–4 Goal: Get both the 6 and the 7 — and keep them!
________________________________
## 🏁 **SETUP** - Deal **2 cards face up** to each player - Put the rest in a pile (**draw pile**) - Flip 1 card to start the **discard pile** - Take turns **clockwise**
________________________________
## 🔄 **YOUR TURN** 1. Pick **1 card** - From the draw pile **or** discard pile 2. Now you have **3 cards** 3. Check the **6–7 Rule** (below) 4. End your turn by discarding **1 card** - Put it in the **discard pile** - OR use a **“Gotcha!” move 😎**
________________________________
## ⚠️ **THE 6–7 RULE** If you have a **6 or 7**: 1. Look at your **other 2 cards** 2. Use **addition (+)** or **subtraction (−)** * If the 2 cards make your number: ❌ lose your 6 or 7 → pass it to the player on your right * If the 2 cards do NOT make your number: ✅ keep it Important: The math must equal the exact card you have, not just any 6 or 7.
________________________________
## 👍 **EXAMPLES** - 6, 2, 4 → 2 + 4 = 6 → ❌ lose the 6 - 7, 5, 2 → 5 + 2 = 7 → ❌ lose the 7 - 6, 2, 5 → 2 + 5 = 7 (not 6) → ✅ keep the 6
________________________________
## 🔁 **PASS-AROUND RULE** - If a player loses a 6 or 7: 1. Pass it to the player on your right 2. If that player also can’t keep it **(because of the 6–7 rule)**, they pass it again 3. The card keeps moving **counterclockwise** 🔄 If the card comes back to the original player in the SAME round: ✅ They may keep the card * But must discard one of their other 2 cards into the middle of the discard pile 👉 This stops the loop so the same combo can’t be used again right away
________________________________
## 😎 **“GOTCHA!” MOVE** - If the player on your left has a 6 or 7: - You may give them a card **instead of discarding** - **Only do this if it will make them lose their 6 or 7**
________________________________
## 🏆 **HOW TO WIN** - Get **both the 6 and the 7** - Keep them until the **end of your turn** - If you don’t lose them… **you win! 🎉**
________________________________
## 💡 **TIP** Try **not** to hold cards that can combine to make your 6 or 7!

	Jacob,

	Thank you for your review and detailed feedback.

	
	We would like to provide clarification regarding the EMD square footage calculation noted in the corrections.

	
	Per the approved Use Permit stipulations, the maximum electronic message display (EMD) area is limited to 40 square feet . Our understanding and intent is that this requirement applies specifically to the programmable message display portion of the sign.

	
	The current design includes:

	*	40 square feet of electronic message display (EMD) used for changeable messaging 
	*	20 square feet of fuel price displays, which are static price changers 

	
	The fuel price components:

	*	Are not used for messaging or advertising 
	*	Do not function as an electronic message center 
	*	Are regulated separately, as fuel pricing is required to be continuously and accurately displayed for operational compliance 

	
	Because of this distinction, the fuel price displays should not be considered part of the EMD area calculation. The EMD portion of the sign remains compliant with the 40 square foot limitation as outlined in the Use Permit.

	
	Additionally, we note that the prior approval did not include stipulations restricting the configuration in this manner , further supporting the interpretation that the EMD limitation applies specifically to the message display portion.

Jacob,

Thank you for your review and detailed feedback.


We would like to provide clarification regarding the EMD square footage calculation noted in the corrections.


Per the approved Use Permit stipulations, the maximum electronic message display (EMD) area is limited to 40 square feet . Our understanding and intent is that this requirement applies specifically to the programmable message display portion of the sign.


The current design includes:

*	40 square feet of electronic message display (EMD) used for changeable messaging 
*	20 square feet of fuel price displays, which are static price changers 


The fuel price components:

*	Are not used for messaging or advertising 
*	Do not function as an electronic message center 
*	Are regulated separately, as fuel pricing is required to be continuously and accurately displayed for operational compliance 


Because of this distinction, the fuel price displays should not be considered part of the EMD area calculation. The EMD portion of the sign remains compliant with the 40 square foot limitation as outlined in the Use Permit.


Additionally, we note that the prior approval did not include stipulations restricting the configuration in this manner , further supporting the interpretation that the EMD limitation applies specifically to the message display portion.


We would appreciate your confirmation on this interpretation so we may proceed accordingly without unnecessary redesign.


Thank you,

 

Steve Skye

Hello,

 

All za approvals are held for a 15-day appeal period. This ends after April 3rd.

 

Please attach the approved use permit document to your project.

Please attach new drawing that show it complies with the use permit stipulations

1.	Maximum EMD sign area is 40 square feet. Drawing show “two full color message units” that total 60 square feet
2.	Drawing electrical details should be certified to not exceed 300 nits of brightness.

 

Previous corrections show requirement for design review. Once drawings have been corrected, please attach your written narrative. Design review fee is still due. Call 602 534 5934 to make payment if you cannot make payment online.

 

Previous corrections show sign falls into a public utility easement. No new documents have been updated to show change of location nor have you provided sign off from every utility company operating in this easement.

 

Previous corrections show this sign has the potential to disturb the approved landscape trees. Any relocation or removal of landscaping requires pdd.siteplanning@phoenix.gov <mailto:pdd.siteplanning@phoenix.gov>  written approval.

 

Please email me when you have addressed all corrections

 

Thank you,

Hi Otis,

subject: city of Buckeye Permit has been issued - BLDC-26-0061
body:
Your permit is now in Issued status, and the approved plans and documents are available online through the Citizen Self-Service (CSS) Portal. Inspections can be scheduled online through the portal. Please follow the instructions below to access, print your permit, and download approved plans.

 

How to Print a Permit 

1.	Log in to the CSS Portal: City of Buckeye <https://egselfservice.buckeyeaz.gov/energov_prod/selfservice#/home>  

	*	Note: Registration is required to access records. If you do not have an account, you must create one before proceeding.

2.	Locate Your Permit: 

	*	Click on the “Dashboard” tab.
	*	Find your permits under “My Permits”, or use the search bar to locate them.
	*	Click the permit record to open the permit details.

3.	Print the Permit: 

	*	Locate and Click the Printer Icon at the top right section of the screen.

 



 

How to Download Approved Plans

1.	Access the Permit Record (Follow Steps 1-2 above)
2.	Go to the “Attachments” tab within the permit record.
3.	Click on each approved file to download.

 

Important Notes:

*	You must be logged in to access permit documents and schedule inspections.
*	If you cannot view your records, please email permitcenter@buckeyeaz.gov <mailto:permitcenter@buckeyeaz.gov>  or call our office at 623-349-6200 for assistance.

subject: Ticket Notifications 202603110552: Item created, triggered per rule: CAD -  Southwest
body:
Ticket Status Notification

Ticket Information

Ticket Number: 2026031101613

Ticket Location: N VERRADO WAY
BUCKEYE, MARICOPA, AZ United States
33.4574620350732, -112.502407151391 

Due Date: 03/13/2026 8:00 PM ET

Company: CHRISTY SIGNS

Phone: 6022424488

Fax/Email:  / STEVE@CHRISTYSIGNS.COM

 




Reason for Notification

Notification Type: Bore Standby        Date: 03/11/2026

You have indicated on the Locate Request(s) that you intend to use Boring in your work area. To ensure the integrity of our system, Southwest Gas is requesting you call us prior to exposing our facilities. Southwest Gas requires a representative to be present to verify our facilities prior to boring across or parallel within 5-feet of Southwest Gas facilities. This is to confirm that you have in fact exposed our line and confirm the line depth to assure a safe bore operation by positive identification of our facilities. Call to schedule a standby a minimum of two hours prior to work identified above.

Notify an SWG representative when boring parallel to any Southwest Gas facilities within 5-feet of the bore. This applies to vertical boring as well.

1.	Notify an SWG representative when boring across any Southwest Gas facilities.

2.	Pothole any gas facilities within 24-inches of the proposed bore path.

3.	Hand digging is required within 24-inches of the gas facility markings, and all gas facilities must be identified, protected, and exposed during any boring operations.

4.	Before the excavation, schedule a Bore Standby with a SWG representative to be present to verify the buried facilities and monitor the boring activities.

Please contact your local SWG field office to schedule a Bore Standby with a Southwest Gas representative a

minimum of 2 hours prior.

 602-484-5086

 For more information regarding safe digging practices, please visit swgas.com

Locate Requester will notify its employees and any of their subcontractors of these requirements.

If you have any questions or need any assistance, please notify Southwest Gas immediately.

Southwest Gas Corporation Business Hours (Mon-Fri between 600 a.m. & 2:30 p.m.) After Hours Emergency: 877-860-6020

EXCAVATOR PRECAUTIONARY GUIDELINES

 

This information is to assist excavators in the proper identification of gas facilities, and precautions to be taken when working around gas facilities.  The information provided here is not to be considered all-inclusive. All excavators digging within the vicinity of gas pipelines must protect the pipelines in accordance with the applicable One-Call law. The following are guidelines that will assist you in protecting the public, you, and the gas facilities.

If any gas pipelines are damaged, federal law requires that you call Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Additionally, if the damage results in the escape of gas, you must call the Emergency Number 911.  Note: Damage includes damage to steel pipeline coatings, gouges in plastic pipe, damaged tracer wire, dents or scrapes in steel pipe, etc.

Gas pipeline markers are used to alert the public that gas pipelines are buried in the general area. These markers may or may not be placed directly over the gas facility. When performing an excavation within 10’ of a “High Pressure” marked facility, please contact SWG to arrange for stand by personnel to be present.

 

PLASTIC PIPELINES:  Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) pipe is one type of plastic pipe used in the SWG gas distribution system.  PVC may be faint yellow, gray or white in color and range in size from ½" to 2" in diameter.  PVC is not as flexible as the polyethylene (PE) pipe that SWG installs today. The integrity of PVC can be compromised if scratched or subjected to external loads and/or stresses.  PE is another type of plastic pipe used in SWG’s system.  PE may be found in various colors and range in size from ½" to 8" in diameter.  Although PE is a more flexible material, its integrity can be compromised if scratched or nicked.  Many plastic gas pipelines are installed with a tracer wire in order to locate the facility.  If a tracer wire is or has been severed or damaged, call SWG.  We will repair the damaged wire at no charge.

 

STEEL PIPELINES: Steel gas pipelines, used in both SWG gas distribution and high-pressure transmission systems, range in size from ½" to 24" in diameter and are also susceptible to damage.  Dents and gouges in the steel will affect the integrity of the pipe, so precautionary measures must be taken during excavation.  Steel pipelines are protected with an approved coating material that helps prevent deterioration of the pipe and can be found in various colors.  If during excavation the coating is torn or damaged, contact SWG immediately to facilitate the repairs at no charge.  Call us before disturbing any mastic coating on active or abandoned steel pipe.  The coating is likely to contain regulated asbestos fibers that can be harmful to your employees.

 

Typically, most gas pipes have specific identification markings on them or on the coating.  Care should be taken to support and protect all gas pipelines, as required by law, when exposed or crossed during excavation activities.  Additionally, care must be taken while exposing existing facilities as they may or may not have padding and shading surrounding them as outlined below.  If any gas pipeline is damaged, call SWG immediately to facilitate the proper pipeline repairs.  When excavations have been completed, gas pipelines must be properly padded, shaded, and backfilled per SWG standards, as shown in the drawing below.  SWG specifications for padding and shading material call for it to be able to sift through a 3/8" screen and be smooth and relatively rock free.  Excavations must be compacted to meet the requirements of local authorities.  During backfill activities it is very important to compact the soil beneath the gas pipe to properly support it. Also, it is important to avoid mechanically compacting the soil directly over the gas pipe to eliminate any unnecessary external stresses.  Steps must be taken during this process to protect the gas pipeline from excessive external loadings.  If other utilities or substructures are to be installed in the same excavation as a gas pipeline, the proper clearances shown in the drawing must be maintained.

If at any time during excavation activities you smell gas, call SWG and 911.

*	DO NOT attempt to control or stop the flow of natural gas, or make repairs.
*	DO NOT turn on, turn off, or attempt to move or operate equipment near the line break or point of leakage.
*	DO NOT enter the area where the natural gas is escaping.
*	DO NOT allow others to enter the area.
*	DO NOT leave the scene of the incident until assistance has arrived.
*	DO secure the area and prevent others from entering.
*	DO eliminate sources of ignition, such as sparks or flames, near the gaseous atmosphere.

For more information on the types of gas pipe used by SWG, positive identification of gas facilities, or if you have any questions, please contact the SWG office nearest you. Additional information on natural gas safety is included in our Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) located at www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .

Please forward to the appropriate excavator.




Esta información tiene como objetivo ayudar a los excavadores a identificar adecuadamente las instalaciones de gas y a conocer las precauciones que deben tener cuando trabajan cerca de ellas. La información aquí provista no es exhaustiva. Todos los excavadores que trabajen en cercanías de gasoductos deben protegerlos de acuerdo con la ley vigente sobre excavaciones. Las siguientes son pautas que lo ayudarán a proteger al público, a usted mismo y a las instalaciones de gas.

Si el gasoducto está dañado, la ley federal exige que llame a Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Además, si el daño causa un escape de gas, debe llamar al número para emergencias 911. Nota: Los daños pueden ser daños en el recubrimiento de las tuberías de acero, aberturas en las tuberías plásticas, daños en el alambre de rastreo, mellas o raspaduras en las tuberías de acero, etc.

 

Se usan señales para advertir al público de que hay gasoductos enterrados en el área. Estas señales pueden ponerse directamente sobre la instalación de gas o no. Cuando se lleva a cabo una excavación dentro de los 10’ de una instalación señalizada como “High Pressure” (de alta presión), comuníquese con SWG para que envíen personal de respaldo.

TUBERÍAS PLÁSTICAS Las tuberías de policloruro de vinilo (PVC) son un tipo de tubería plástica que SWG usa en el sistema de distribución. Las tuberías de PVC pueden ser de color amarillo claro, gris o blanco, y su tamaño puede ir desde ½” hasta 2” de diámetro. Las tuberías de PVC no son tan flexibles como las de polietileno (PE) que SWG instala hoy. El PVC puede arruinarse si se raya o se somete a pesos o tensiones extremos. Las tuberías de PE son otro tipo de tuberías plásticas que SWG usa en su sistema. Las tuberías de PE pueden ser de varios colores, y su tamaño va desde ½” hasta 8” de diámetro. Aunque el PE es un material más flexible, puede arruinarse si se raya o corta. Muchos gasoductos de plástico se instalan con un alambre de rastreo para ubicar la instalación. Si el alambre de rastreo se corta o daña, llame a SWG. Lo repararemos sin cargo.

 

TUBERÍAS DE ACERO Las tuberías de gas de acero, usadas por SWG tanto para la distribución de gas como para los sistemas de transmisión a alta presión, varían en tamaño desde 1/2" hasta 24" de diámetro y también son susceptibles a los daños. Las mellas y aberturas en el acero pueden afectar la integridad de la tubería. Por eso, deben tomarse medidas de precaución durante la excavación. Las tuberías de acero se protegen con un material de recubrimiento aprobado que ayuda a prevenir su deterioro y puede ser de varios colores. Si durante la excavación el recubrimiento se desprende o daña, comuníquese con SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones sin cargo. Llámenos antes de quitar cualquier recubrimiento de masilla de una tubería de acero activa o abandonada. Es posible que el recubrimiento contenga fibras de amianto reglamentario que pueden ser dañinas para sus empleados.

 

En general, las tuberías de gas tienen marcas de identificación específicas sobre ellas o sobre el recubrimiento. Debe tenerse precaución y sostener y proteger todos los gasoductos, según lo requiera la ley, cuando se expongan o crucen durante la excavación. Además, debe tenerse cuidado al exponer instalaciones existentes, ya que pueden o no, tener relleno a su alrededor, como se detalla más abajo. Si un gasoducto está dañado, llame a SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones necesarias. Cuando finalicen las excavaciones, los gasoductos deben ser rellenados según las normas de SWG, como se muestra en el dibujo más abajo. Las especificaciones de SWG para el material de relleno indican que este debe poder pasar a través de un tamiz de 3/8”, ser suave y estar relativamente libre de escombros.  Las excavaciones deben ser compactadas para cumplir con los requisitos de las autoridades locales. Durante el rellenado, es muy importante compactar el suelo bajo el gasoducto, a fin de sujetarlo apropiadamente. También es importante evitar compactar mecánicamente el suelo que está sobre el gasoducto para eliminar tensiones externas innecesarias. Deben tomarse medidas durante este proceso para proteger el gasoducto de cargas externas excesivas. Si se deben instalar otros servicios o subestructuras en la misma excavación del gasoducto, deben respetarse las distancias que se muestran en el dibujo.

Si en cualquier momento durante la excavación percibe olor a gas, llame a SWG y al 911.

*	NO intente controlar ni parar el flujo de gas natural ni de hacer reparaciones.
*	NO encienda, apague ni intente mover u operar equipos cerca del punto donde se rompió la línea o se produjo el escape.
*	NO entre en un área donde haya un escape de gas natural.
*	NO permita que otras personas entren en dicha área.
*	NO deje el lugar del incidente hasta que llegue la ayuda.
*	DESPEJE el área y evite que otras personas entren en ella.
*	ELIMINE las fuentes de combustión, como chispas o llamas, cerca de la atmósfera gaseosa.

Si desea más información sobre los tipos de tuberías de gas usados por SWG o sobre cómo identificar instalaciones de gas, o si tiene preguntas, llame a la oficina de SWG más cercana. En nuestra hoja de datos de seguridad de material (MSDS), puede encontrar más información sobre la seguridad con el gas natural. Esta se encuentra en www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .






Favor de hacer llegar al excavador correspondiente.

The coating is likely to contain regulated asbestos fibers that can be harmful to your employees.

 

Typically, most gas pipes have specific identification markings on them or on the coating.  Care should be taken to support and protect all gas pipelines, as required by law, when exposed or crossed during excavation activities.  Additionally, care must be taken while exposing existing facilities as they may or may not have padding and shading surrounding them as outlined below.  If any gas pipeline is damaged, call SWG immediately to facilitate the proper pipeline repairs.  When excavations have been completed, gas pipelines must be properly padded, shaded, and backfilled per SWG standards, as shown in the drawing below.  SWG specifications for padding and shading material call for it to be able to sift through a 3/8" screen and be smooth and relatively rock free.  Excavations must be compacted to meet the requirements of local authorities.  During backfill activities it is very important to compact the soil beneath the gas pipe to properly support it. Also, it is important to avoid mechanically compacting the soil directly over the gas pipe to eliminate any unnecessary external stresses.  Steps must be taken during this process to protect the gas pipeline from excessive external loadings.  If other utilities or substructures are to be installed in the same excavation as a gas pipeline, the proper clearances shown in the drawing must be maintained.

If at any time during excavation activities you smell gas, call SWG and 911.

*	DO NOT attempt to control or stop the flow of natural gas, or make repairs.
*	DO NOT turn on, turn off, or attempt to move or operate equipment near the line break or point of leakage.
*	DO NOT enter the area where the natural gas is escaping.
*	DO NOT allow others to enter the area.
*	DO NOT leave the scene of the incident until assistance has arrived.
*	DO secure the area and prevent others from entering.
*	DO eliminate sources of ignition, such as sparks or flames, near the gaseous atmosphere.

For more information on the types of gas pipe used by SWG, positive identification of gas facilities, or if you have any questions, please contact the SWG office nearest you. Additional information on natural gas safety is included in our Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) located at www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .

Please forward to the appropriate excavator.




Esta información tiene como objetivo ayudar a los excavadores a identificar adecuadamente las instalaciones de gas y a conocer las precauciones que deben tener cuando trabajan cerca de ellas. La información aquí provista no es exhaustiva. Todos los excavadores que trabajen en cercanías de gasoductos deben protegerlos de acuerdo con la ley vigente sobre excavaciones. Las siguientes son pautas que lo ayudarán a proteger al público, a usted mismo y a las instalaciones de gas.

Si el gasoducto está dañado, la ley federal exige que llame a Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Además, si el daño causa un escape de gas, debe llamar al número para emergencias 911. Nota: Los daños pueden ser daños en el recubrimiento de las tuberías de acero, aberturas en las tuberías plásticas, daños en el alambre de rastreo, mellas o raspaduras en las tuberías de acero, etc.

 

Se usan señales para advertir al público de que hay gasoductos enterrados en el área. Estas señales pueden ponerse directamente sobre la instalación de gas o no. Cuando se lleva a cabo una excavación dentro de los 10’ de una instalación señalizada como “High Pressure” (de alta presión), comuníquese con SWG para que envíen personal de respaldo.

TUBERÍAS PLÁSTICAS Las tuberías de policloruro de vinilo (PVC) son un tipo de tubería plástica que SWG usa en el sistema de distribución. Las tuberías de PVC pueden ser de color amarillo claro, gris o blanco, y su tamaño puede ir desde ½” hasta 2” de diámetro. Las tuberías de PVC no son tan flexibles como las de polietileno (PE) que SWG instala hoy. El PVC puede arruinarse si se raya o se somete a pesos o tensiones extremos. Las tuberías de PE son otro tipo de tuberías plásticas que SWG usa en su sistema. Las tuberías de PE pueden ser de varios colores, y su tamaño va desde ½” hasta 8” de diámetro. Aunque el PE es un material más flexible, puede arruinarse si se raya o corta. Muchos gasoductos de plástico se instalan con un alambre de rastreo para ubicar la instalación. Si el alambre de rastreo se corta o daña, llame a SWG. Lo repararemos sin cargo.

 

TUBERÍAS DE ACERO Las tuberías de gas de acero, usadas por SWG tanto para la distribución de gas como para los sistemas de transmisión a alta presión, varían en tamaño desde 1/2" hasta 24" de diámetro y también son susceptibles a los daños. Las mellas y aberturas en el acero pueden afectar la integridad de la tubería. Por eso, deben tomarse medidas de precaución durante la excavación. Las tuberías de acero se protegen con un material de recubrimiento aprobado que ayuda a prevenir su deterioro y puede ser de varios colores. Si durante la excavación el recubrimiento se desprende o daña, comuníquese con SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones sin cargo. Llámenos antes de quitar cualquier recubrimiento de masilla de una tubería de acero activa o abandonada. Es posible que el recubrimiento contenga fibras de amianto reglamentario que pueden ser dañinas para sus empleados.

 

En general, las tuberías de gas tienen marcas de identificación específicas sobre ellas o sobre el recubrimiento. Debe tenerse precaución y sostener y proteger todos los gasoductos, según lo requiera la ley, cuando se expongan o crucen durante la excavación. Además, debe tenerse cuidado al exponer instalaciones existentes, ya que pueden o no, tener relleno a su alrededor, como se detalla más abajo. Si un gasoducto está dañado, llame a SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones necesarias. Cuando finalicen las excavaciones, los gasoductos deben ser rellenados según las normas de SWG, como se muestra en el dibujo más abajo. Las especificaciones de SWG para el material de relleno indican que este debe poder pasar a través de un tamiz de 3/8”, ser suave y estar relativamente libre de escombros.  Las excavaciones deben ser compactadas para cumplir con los requisitos de las autoridades locales. Durante el rellenado, es muy importante compactar el suelo bajo el gasoducto, a fin de sujetarlo apropiadamente. También es importante evitar compactar mecánicamente el suelo que está sobre el gasoducto para eliminar tensiones externas innecesarias. Deben tomarse medidas durante este proceso para proteger el gasoducto de cargas externas excesivas. Si se deben instalar otros servicios o subestructuras en la misma excavación del gasoducto, deben respetarse las distancias que se muestran en el dibujo.

Si en cualquier momento durante la excavación percibe olor a gas, llame a SWG y al 911.

*	NO intente controlar ni parar el flujo de gas natural ni de hacer reparaciones.
*	NO encienda, apague ni intente mover u operar equipos cerca del punto donde se rompió la línea o se produjo el escape.
*	NO entre en un área donde haya un escape de gas natural.
*	NO permita que otras personas entren en dicha área.
*	NO deje el lugar del incidente hasta que llegue la ayuda.
*	DESPEJE el área y evite que otras personas entren en ella.
*	ELIMINE las fuentes de combustión, como chispas o llamas, cerca de la atmósfera gaseosa.

Si desea más información sobre los tipos de tuberías de gas usados por SWG o sobre cómo identificar instalaciones de gas, o si tiene preguntas, llame a la oficina de SWG más cercana. En nuestra hoja de datos de seguridad de material (MSDS), puede encontrar más información sobre la seguridad con el gas natural. Esta se encuentra en www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .






Favor de hacer llegar al excavador correspondiente.

Hi Taryn,

I wanted to follow up regarding PMT26-01022 – Sherwin-Williams (1202 University Dr.) and your correction comment under §11-43-2B1.a.i or ii.

We recently spoke with a Planner of the Day, who reviewed the proposed sign plans and recognized that the signs are pan-channel letters mounted on a backer panel, not cabinet signs. 

This configuration itself appears to meet the intent of §11-43-2B1.a.i (individual letters), but we understand that the current plan set did not clearly communicate that distinction.


To clarify the construction method, we are providing the attached channel letter installation cut sheet, which demonstrates how the pan-channel letters are mounted and wired, including attachment and structural details. This should eliminate any ambiguity regarding the sign type and confirm that it is not a standard rectangular cabinet.


Please let us know if this documentation will satisfy the review requirement, or if you would like us to incorporate additional clarification directly into the plan set for resubmittal.

Also, we need assistance in uploading them via the portal.


Thank you for your time and review.


Best regards,

In partnership with

 <https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/cxcShT1y9bsE5DeUu6c%2F7LnJO%2BuMoN5rlBAiTjd6sArK%2F4rWZtfrY9bQjZge%0Ar29JmXGnGmDFvvgRai2%2BkBiDuuqsWcVHGIFAGE3yEaOqXD7ZtAd1w1onYQVK%0AcawQ6sRI%2BAoi7ug77XeaTXMJiOZIa5Trl19bUPahQIMV0SDyNUuG%2BS2zLlb0%0AZ58M%2BwMi1Qg2e5tT2TQZxmIu8bZYYouVLppX64v1EpdVYsH8KaIstkQW7hCQ%0AxE3gNIhstXd9C%2FTzvDAhynEBE%2BaA32mGAPCMKpCTbPDn7enzABPaBMCVEm0%3D%0A/35e33aff5c43d276> 	
 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8ca971cf-c92f-4689-a1dc-900919ac6f73/Eyebrows.png?t=1760976197> 	
 

  	Dear Readers,

Google just mass-democratized AI performance, and the price tag is almost laughable. Their new Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite delivers speeds 2.5x faster than its predecessor at just $0.25 per million input tokens, proving that cutting-edge intelligence no longer demands a cutting-edge budget.

But that's just the opener today: Apple is fusing two 3nm dies into a single chip with the M5 Pro and M5 Max, rewriting what a laptop can do for AI workloads. OpenAI quietly shipped GPT-5.3 Instant with a 26.8% reduction in hallucinations, and Microsoft is betting Windows 12's future on an AI-first modular architecture that could lock out millions of current PCs.

Meanwhile, a brilliantly simple benchmark called BullshitBench v2 reveals an uncomfortable truth: most AI models would rather confidently make things up than simply say "I don't know," and only a handful actually pass the test. Grab your coffee, this one's packed.

In Today’s Issue:

⚡ Google drops Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite, a blazing-fast new model

💻 Apple merges two 3nm dies to create the M5 Pro and M5 Max

💬 OpenAI quietly ships GPT-5.3 Instant to slash ChatGPT hallucinations by 26.8%

🪟 Microsoft prepares AI-driven Windows 12 that could lock out millions of older PCs without a dedicated NPU

🛑 Most top-tier AI models would rather confidently hallucinate than admit they don't know the answer

✨ And more AI goodness…

All the best,

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/c82900b7-ebbf-4eb6-811f-86a9b3dac911/image.png?t=1756137355> 	
  	
  	
 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7b665c8b-a655-4dd2-89d3-61bc24b2ab7e/Button.png?t=1760609218> 	
  	 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/f509b114-7eb9-43a3-8a8e-6bfb203a19bc/Eyebrows.png?t=1760708829> 	
 

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/399c398c-49e5-40d7-82d9-7b726aaf9c8b/Image_Aspect_Ratio.png?t=1772643042> 	
 


🚀 Apple Unleashes M5 Powerhouse Chips

Apple has introduced the M5 Pro and M5 Max, built on a new Fusion Architecture that merges two 3nm dies into a single SoC, unlocking up to 30% faster CPU performance and over 4x peak GPU compute for AI versus the previous generation. With an 18-core CPU (6 “super cores”), up to a 40-core GPU featuring Neural Accelerators, and unified memory bandwidth reaching 614GB/s, these chips are engineered for serious pro workflows, from 3D rendering to large language models.

For creators, developers, and AI researchers, this means up to 35% better ray tracing graphics, 2.5x multithreaded gains over the M1 Pro/Max, and configurations supporting up to 128GB unified memory, turning the new MacBook Pro into a next-level performance machine, available March 11.

Learn More <https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/VWYEkTZzmm8q4e7A1Buzarw5Wmfix72QApjvkVvIZ2GbT6Xnbq2DPLJWduZM%0ATvbl9ZMSgfvDsjUhgyhzGkcZzfSmx%2BQ5ice9DfzkULdLofud6aZtNOJxk32h%0AqPrGxtWHbw4Ndmqr2CIdMWEwSFvF7M6YgKh26h9m%2Bbkld1ofnvs%3D%0A/275b9884fdc42b91> 	
 

 <https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/oZ1aDP2s4jIR2VRSv5ePoaqJTb9ygcqNL6Zmhx2fKx0sKmpq39neDkBdXnW0%0AZjL59KmIws6zizNcguqPYPGxNj5EyaJCh2TV8OQdg588lzceuuTF6Hi%2BwiWK%0AnV79ud5LRGwumhkwda%2F5pcdCu98jxAkdwnofMdDX%2BZT4KsloyfY%3D%0A/f9b57af0a0f23f46> 	
 


🚀 GPT-5.3 Instant Improves ChatGPT Conversations

OpenAI has released GPT-5.3 Instant, an upgrade to ChatGPT’s most-used model that focuses on smoother conversations, fewer unnecessary refusals, and more accurate responses. The update reduces hallucinations by up to 26.8%, improves web-based answers by better synthesizing search results with the model’s knowledge, and removes overly cautious disclaimers that previously interrupted responses.

Overall, the goal is simple: make everyday interactions feel more natural, relevant, and helpful, with clearer answers, better writing ability, and a conversational tone that flows more smoothly for users. OpenAI has already announced the next major update to version 5.4.

Learn More <https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/zIV%2BOLmgNGnlBBI1vnSV4%2FT960J2cRabyt2RvEQC2m236y9bQOg4wEQdR32x%0A35j53emoZd3vu8y%2BMZnW4IWaGOaOqJXfTSv0%2FwQFkDsfG7P6oT5G0q7zUTxB%0AgTaj21wejAF%2B4AgzJdIwrgIzmD%2F5PGwDR73fsiJ2%2Be%2FT9rkLUMk%3D%0A/5ff5da3b66bec306> 	

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/844b108e-8ef4-4146-b90c-0c97f77d5bb4/Image_Aspect_Ratio__1_.png?t=1772643207> 	
 


🚀 Windows 12 AI-Driven Modular OS

Microsoft is reportedly preparing to launch Windows 12 later in 2026, built around a modular CorePC architecture that lets users customize the OS by adding or removing components for different needs like gaming or lightweight systems. Google Drops a Speed Monster, And It Costs Almost Nothing

The Takeaway

👉 Google's Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite delivers 2.5x faster response times and 45% higher output speed than its predecessor at a fraction of the cost, $0.25 per million input tokens makes it the most affordable model in the Gemini 3 series.

👉 Adjustable thinking levels give developers granular control over the speed-quality tradeoff, enabling cost optimization for high-volume tasks like translation and moderation while preserving reasoning power for complex workloads.

👉 With an Elo score of 1432 and benchmark results surpassing larger previous-generation Gemini models, Flash-Lite signals that the performance gap between "budget" and "premium" AI tiers is collapsing fast.

👉 Early adopters including Latitude, Cartwheel, and Whering report that Flash-Lite handles complex inputs with precision comparable to larger models - enterprise teams should evaluate whether their current model spend is still justified.

Google just made powerful AI absurdly affordable. The company launched Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite, the fastest and cheapest model in its entire Gemini 3 lineup, and the benchmarks are turning heads. Priced at just $0.25 per million input tokens and $1.50 per million output tokens, this model delivers performance that used to require models costing eight times as much.

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/848d66b8-2d13-485e-ad50-a3078217226b/Outline__2_.png?t=1772644085> 	
 

Here's what makes it exciting: Flash-Lite responds 2.5 times faster than its predecessor, Gemini 2.5 Flash, while also producing 45% more tokens per second. That's not an incremental upgrade, that's a generational leap. It scored 1432 Elo on the Arena.ai Leaderboard, beat larger Gemini models on reasoning benchmarks, and nailed 86.9% on GPQA Diamond. For a "Lite" model, it punches way above its weight.

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/25f41aca-232d-4b6c-bd13-1962dcab08c2/Outline__1_.png?t=1772644097> 	
 

What really sets it apart is adjustable thinking levels. Developers can dial reasoning up or down depending on the task: fast and cheap for content moderation, deeper for complex UI generation. Companies like Latitude, Cartwheel, and Whering are already running it in production.

Why it matters: Google's Flash-Lite proves that cutting-edge AI performance no longer requires cutting-edge budgets. This shift toward affordable, high-speed intelligence at scale could fundamentally reshape how startups and enterprises approach AI deployment, making sophisticated AI accessible to teams and use cases that were previously priced out.

AI Models Can't Say "No"

Most AI models have a people-pleasing problem, and now there's data to prove it. BullshitBench v2, created by Peter Gostev, is a benchmark that does something refreshingly different: it tests whether AI models can detect and reject nonsensical prompts instead of confidently rolling with them. Think of it as a BS detector for AI.

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9a8f2837-c0b8-4093-9908-a588900e3fc8/Outline__4_.png?t=1772644587> 	

The v2 update brings 100 new questions across five domains: coding, medical, legal, finance, and physics, with over 70 model variants tested. The questions are cleverly designed to sound authoritative while being completely made up. Imagine asking a model about measuring "milliempathies" in nurses or calculating the "activation energy" of a non-compete clause. Sounds legit, right? That's the trap.

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/22d27930-25f2-40fc-83ee-e8b72cc52f41/Outline__6_.png?t=1772644540> 	

The results are striking: only Anthropic's Claude models and Alibaba's Qwen 3.5 score meaningfully above 60% on nonsense detection. OpenAI and Google? Stuck, and not improving. Even more surprising: reasoning models that "think harder" actually perform worse. They use their extra compute to rationalize the nonsense rather than reject it.

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e80ba2d7-089c-4a73-a707-bcdf2f93892d/Outline__5_.png?t=1772644401> 	

BullshitBench v2 is one of the few benchmarks where most models are not getting better over time, exposing a fundamental gap between appearing smart and being reliable.
