Subject: RE: Crumbl–Peoria - Allowed Sign Area Confirmation (01/16/26) 

 

Hi Sarah,

Thanks for the question — this is a good one.


I reviewed both the City of Phoenix Sign Ordinance and the Metro Towne Center Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP) to confirm the allowable sign area for this location.


Although the tenant frontage is approximately 25 feet, the City of Phoenix code provides a minimum wall sign allowance of 50 square feet for commercial tenants. This comes directly from Phoenix Sign Ordinance Table D-1, which states:

“Wall Signs – Commercial: 1 square foot of sign area per 1 linear foot of building frontage (minimum 50 square feet).”


Because the ordinance establishes a 50 sq ft minimum, the normal frontage-based calculation (25 LF = 25 sq ft) does not apply here.


The Metro Towne Center CSP does not reduce this allowance — it regulates sign type and design standards, not overall area. The CSP permits aluminum pan channel letters for shop tenants and defers to the city ordinance for allowable square footage.  Based on both the Phoenix Sign Ordinance and the CSP:

• The maximum allowable area for the Crumbl primary wall sign is 50 square feet
• This allowance applies even with a 25’ tenant frontage
• Flush-mounted channel letters up to 50 sq ft total are permitted


You can therefore size the letters and logo however needed, provided the overall sign copy fits within a 50 sq ft envelope.


Please let us know if able to be of any additional assistance.


Warm regards,

Steve - CRUMBL will not allow the backer panel to be anything but pink so will have to change these over to flush mounted letters.  What is the square footage allowed so I can determine what size letters.  

 

Thank you!

Cc: Scott Frazer <scott@christysigns.com <mailto:scott@christysigns.com> >
Subject: RE: Crumbl – Metro Towne Center CSP Review & Design Direction (01/13/26) 

 

Sarah,


Yes — your understanding is correct.


Under the Metro Towne Center CSP, the key requirement is that the sign copy be aluminum pan channel letters and not a cabinet-style sign box. 

The CSP does not prohibit raceways or backer panels — it regulates the sign type, not whether the letters are mounted directly to the wall, to a mesh raceway, or to a solid raceway.


Tropical Smoothie is a good example of this. Their sign uses individual channel letters mounted to a solid raceway, which is allowed under the CSP, just as the mesh-style raceways used by Supercuts, Pizza Patrón, and Dickey’s are allowed. Crumbl can follow either approach.


So, for Crumbl:

*	The letters must be individual aluminum pan channel letters

I reviewed both the City of Phoenix Sign Ordinance and the Metro Towne Center Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP) to confirm the allowable sign area for this location.


Although the tenant frontage is approximately 25 feet, the City of Phoenix code provides a minimum wall sign allowance of 50 square feet for commercial tenants. This comes directly from Phoenix Sign Ordinance Table D-1, which states:



“Wall Signs – Commercial: 1 square foot of sign area per 1 linear foot of building frontage (minimum 50 square feet).”


Because the ordinance establishes a 50 sq ft minimum, the normal frontage-based calculation (25 LF = 25 sq ft) does not apply here.


The Metro Towne Center CSP does not reduce this allowance — it regulates sign type and design standards, not overall area. The CSP permits aluminum pan channel letters for shop tenants and defers to the city ordinance for allowable square footage.  Based on both the Phoenix Sign Ordinance and the CSP:



• The maximum allowable area for the Crumbl primary wall sign is 50 square feet
• This allowance applies even with a 25’ tenant frontage
• Flush-mounted channel letters up to 50 sq ft total are permitted


You can therefore size the letters and logo however needed, provided the overall sign copy fits within a 50 sq ft envelope.

Hi Jay,

Hi Eric – good to connect again!


Since the previous signs were non-illuminated, there is a strong likelihood that power will need to be brought to each sign location.

Based on the building type, this appears to be a parapet roof condition. In most cases like this, electrical is routed above the roofline, with the junction box located behind the parapet at each sign location so it remains concealed.


To recap the requirements for the illuminated channel letters:

• A junction box must be located within approximately 6 feet of each sign.
• Each sign requires its own dedicated 120V, 20-amp circuit.
• A photocell can be installed at the junction box, or a timer can be installed at the panel to control both displays.


Our installation crew will make the final connection at the sign once proper power is in place.


Eric, if helpful, I’m happy to stop by and review the roof condition before you have someone quote the work. That way the electrician has clear direction on where to terminate the circuits.


Let me know how you’d like to proceed.

• A junction box must be located within approximately 6 feet of each sign.
• Each sign requires its own dedicated 120V, 20-amp circuit.

Our installation crew will make the final connection at the sign once proper power is in place.

subject: Town of Gilbert -  SIGN-2025-00341 Your Permit is Now Available
body:
Your approved permit is attached. Visit our OneStopShop <https://onestopshop.gilbertaz.gov/>  portal to download any approved plans. These can be viewed under the “attachments” section of your permit. Approved plans and permit must be printed and available at the time of your inspections. 

To print a copy of your permit, please use the printer icon in OneStopShop to print your permit. If you do not see the printer icon and your permit is in an "Issued" status, please contact us at EplanBuilding@gilbertaz.gov. 

A one-time registration is required. If you have not already registered, please use this link <https://onestopshop.gilbertaz.gov/>  to do so. Please allow one business day following your registration to gain full access to the OneStopShop portal. 

You will also be able to request inspections as well as monitor inspection results. The OneStopShop is also available for online payments and to apply for future permits. 

For any questions, please call our Development Services team (480) 503-6700, Mon-Thurs 7am-6pm. Offices are closed Fridays and Holidays. 

Thank you, 

Town of Gilbert
Development Services
Ph: 480-503-6700

*We are transitioning online applications from our current ePlan Review to OneStopShop. OneStopShop online applications are currently limited to select permit types: Commercial and Residential Trade permits, Swimming pools, Engineering Utility Permits, Deferred Submittals and Plan Changes. All others must be applied for through our ePlan Review <http://general.gilbertaz.gov/eforms/eplan/BLDGSubmits/ePlanAppConst.cfm>  process.

subject: Town of Gilbert SIGN-2025-00341 Sign permit issued
body:
Dear Customer, 

Thank you for obtaining your permit for your signage here in Gilbert. Please be aware you will need to schedule and complete all applicable inspections relating to this permit. Approved plans must be on-site at the time of your inspection. Please login to our OneStopShop <https://onestopshop.gilbertaz.gov/>  to print your approved plans, pay fees and schedule all inspections. Approved plans can be viewed/printed under the “attachments” section of your permit. 

At this time your scheduled inspection may be eligible for either an onsite or virtual inspection*. The area inspector will contact you if your inspection is eligible to be conducted virtually, otherwise your onsite inspection will be completed as scheduled.

Approved plans and permit must be printed and available at the time of your inspection(s).

For any questions, please call our Development Services team (480) 503-6700, Mon-Thurs 7am-6pm. Offices are closed Fridays and Holidays.

Thank you, 
Town of Gilbert
Development Services
Ph: 480-503-6700 

*For Virtual Inspections, you will need to have the following items:
1.) Measuring tape
2.) Copy of permit application and plans indicating proper distancing and location of sign 
3.) Phone availability of either Facetime, Zoom, Teams or another software program that will allow face to face interaction with the inspector.

subject: Dig Safely Near Southwest Gas Pipelines
body:
DO NOT RESPOND TO THIS EMAIL. For any questions about your one call ticket, please contact your local call center.

STEVE SKYE,

THANK YOU for using 811 to submit a locate ticket for work near Southwest Gas pipelines. 

To help you avoid pipeline emergencies, follow these simple steps:

1.    Survey and mark your proposed dig area with white paint.

2.    Wait the required time. This is 2 working days, NOT including the date of notification.

3.    Respect the marks. Ensure all utility owners have responded before digging.  

4.   Contact Southwest Gas and request a monitor prior to bore operations or working within 10 ft. of high-pressure facilities. 

5.   Dig Carefully.  Watch this short video <https://www.swgas.com/en/excavator-safety?utm_source=link&utm_medium=website_email&utm_campaign=Damage_Prevention_Safe_Digging_Video&utm_id=Perseverant&utm_term=>  to learn best practices when digging around underground natural gas lines.

6.    Follow safe excavation laws for the state you're working in. 

Always dig with care! Damage to natural gas lines can result in costly repairs, service outages, and project downtime, as well as severe injury and/or death.  

To report a pipeline emergency or odor of natural gas, call 911 and Southwest Gas at 877-860-6020.

Thanks for working safely near our facilities.

body:
Ticket Status Notification

Ticket Information

Ticket Number: 2026022701182

Ticket Location: 205 S 99TH AVE
TOLLESON, MARICOPA, AZ United States
33.4484526019032, -112.272188196773 

Due Date: 03/03/2026 7:00 PM ET

Company: CHRISTY SIGNS

Phone: 6022424488

Fax/Email:  / STEVE@CHRISTYSIGNS.COM

 




Reason for Notification

Notification Type: Bore Standby        Date: 02/27/2026

You have indicated on the Locate Request(s) that you intend to use Boring in your work area. To ensure the integrity of our system, Southwest Gas is requesting you call us prior to exposing our facilities. Southwest Gas requires a representative to be present to verify our facilities prior to boring across or parallel within 5-feet of Southwest Gas facilities. This is to confirm that you have in fact exposed our line and confirm the line depth to assure a safe bore operation by positive identification of our facilities. Call to schedule a standby a minimum of two hours prior to work identified above.

Notify an SWG representative when boring parallel to any Southwest Gas facilities within 5-feet of the bore. This applies to vertical boring as well.

1.	Notify an SWG representative when boring across any Southwest Gas facilities.

2.	Pothole any gas facilities within 24-inches of the proposed bore path.

3.	Hand digging is required within 24-inches of the gas facility markings, and all gas facilities must be identified, protected, and exposed during any boring operations.

4.	Before the excavation, schedule a Bore Standby with a SWG representative to be present to verify the buried facilities and monitor the boring activities.

Please contact your local SWG field office to schedule a Bore Standby with a Southwest Gas representative a

minimum of 2 hours prior.

 602-484-5086

 For more information regarding safe digging practices, please visit swgas.com

Locate Requester will notify its employees and any of their subcontractors of these requirements.

If you have any questions or need any assistance, please notify Southwest Gas immediately.

Southwest Gas Corporation Business Hours (Mon-Fri between 600 a.m. & 2:30 p.m.) After Hours Emergency: 877-860-6020

EXCAVATOR PRECAUTIONARY GUIDELINES

 

This information is to assist excavators in the proper identification of gas facilities, and precautions to be taken when working around gas facilities.  The information provided here is not to be considered all-inclusive. All excavators digging within the vicinity of gas pipelines must protect the pipelines in accordance with the applicable One-Call law. The following are guidelines that will assist you in protecting the public, you, and the gas facilities.

If any gas pipelines are damaged, federal law requires that you call Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Additionally, if the damage results in the escape of gas, you must call the Emergency Number 911.  Note: Damage includes damage to steel pipeline coatings, gouges in plastic pipe, damaged tracer wire, dents or scrapes in steel pipe, etc.

Gas pipeline markers are used to alert the public that gas pipelines are buried in the general area. These markers may or may not be placed directly over the gas facility. When performing an excavation within 10’ of a “High Pressure” marked facility, please contact SWG to arrange for stand by personnel to be present.

 

PLASTIC PIPELINES:  Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) pipe is one type of plastic pipe used in the SWG gas distribution system.  PVC may be faint yellow, gray or white in color and range in size from ½" to 2" in diameter.  PVC is not as flexible as the polyethylene (PE) pipe that SWG installs today. The integrity of PVC can be compromised if scratched or subjected to external loads and/or stresses.  PE is another type of plastic pipe used in SWG’s system.  PE may be found in various colors and range in size from ½" to 8" in diameter.  Although PE is a more flexible material, its integrity can be compromised if scratched or nicked.  Many plastic gas pipelines are installed with a tracer wire in order to locate the facility.  If a tracer wire is or has been severed or damaged, call SWG.  We will repair the damaged wire at no charge.

 

STEEL PIPELINES: Steel gas pipelines, used in both SWG gas distribution and high-pressure transmission systems, range in size from ½" to 24" in diameter and are also susceptible to damage.  Dents and gouges in the steel will affect the integrity of the pipe, so precautionary measures must be taken during excavation.  Steel pipelines are protected with an approved coating material that helps prevent deterioration of the pipe and can be found in various colors.  If during excavation the coating is torn or damaged, contact SWG immediately to facilitate the repairs at no charge.  Call us before disturbing any mastic coating on active or abandoned steel pipe.  The coating is likely to contain regulated asbestos fibers that can be harmful to your employees.

 

Typically, most gas pipes have specific identification markings on them or on the coating.  Care should be taken to support and protect all gas pipelines, as required by law, when exposed or crossed during excavation activities.  Additionally, care must be taken while exposing existing facilities as they may or may not have padding and shading surrounding them as outlined below.  If any gas pipeline is damaged, call SWG immediately to facilitate the proper pipeline repairs.  When excavations have been completed, gas pipelines must be properly padded, shaded, and backfilled per SWG standards, as shown in the drawing below.  SWG specifications for padding and shading material call for it to be able to sift through a 3/8" screen and be smooth and relatively rock free.  Excavations must be compacted to meet the requirements of local authorities.  During backfill activities it is very important to compact the soil beneath the gas pipe to properly support it. Also, it is important to avoid mechanically compacting the soil directly over the gas pipe to eliminate any unnecessary external stresses.  Steps must be taken during this process to protect the gas pipeline from excessive external loadings.  If other utilities or substructures are to be installed in the same excavation as a gas pipeline, the proper clearances shown in the drawing must be maintained.

If at any time during excavation activities you smell gas, call SWG and 911.

*	DO NOT attempt to control or stop the flow of natural gas, or make repairs.
*	DO NOT turn on, turn off, or attempt to move or operate equipment near the line break or point of leakage.
*	DO NOT enter the area where the natural gas is escaping.
*	DO NOT allow others to enter the area.
*	DO NOT leave the scene of the incident until assistance has arrived.
*	DO secure the area and prevent others from entering.
*	DO eliminate sources of ignition, such as sparks or flames, near the gaseous atmosphere.

For more information on the types of gas pipe used by SWG, positive identification of gas facilities, or if you have any questions, please contact the SWG office nearest you. Additional information on natural gas safety is included in our Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) located at www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .

Please forward to the appropriate excavator.




Esta información tiene como objetivo ayudar a los excavadores a identificar adecuadamente las instalaciones de gas y a conocer las precauciones que deben tener cuando trabajan cerca de ellas. La información aquí provista no es exhaustiva. Todos los excavadores que trabajen en cercanías de gasoductos deben protegerlos de acuerdo con la ley vigente sobre excavaciones. Las siguientes son pautas que lo ayudarán a proteger al público, a usted mismo y a las instalaciones de gas.

Si el gasoducto está dañado, la ley federal exige que llame a Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Además, si el daño causa un escape de gas, debe llamar al número para emergencias 911. Nota: Los daños pueden ser daños en el recubrimiento de las tuberías de acero, aberturas en las tuberías plásticas, daños en el alambre de rastreo, mellas o raspaduras en las tuberías de acero, etc.

 

Se usan señales para advertir al público de que hay gasoductos enterrados en el área. Estas señales pueden ponerse directamente sobre la instalación de gas o no. Cuando se lleva a cabo una excavación dentro de los 10’ de una instalación señalizada como “High Pressure” (de alta presión), comuníquese con SWG para que envíen personal de respaldo.

TUBERÍAS PLÁSTICAS Las tuberías de policloruro de vinilo (PVC) son un tipo de tubería plástica que SWG usa en el sistema de distribución. Las tuberías de PVC pueden ser de color amarillo claro, gris o blanco, y su tamaño puede ir desde ½” hasta 2” de diámetro. Las tuberías de PVC no son tan flexibles como las de polietileno (PE) que SWG instala hoy. El PVC puede arruinarse si se raya o se somete a pesos o tensiones extremos. Las tuberías de PE son otro tipo de tuberías plásticas que SWG usa en su sistema. Las tuberías de PE pueden ser de varios colores, y su tamaño va desde ½” hasta 8” de diámetro. Aunque el PE es un material más flexible, puede arruinarse si se raya o corta. Muchos gasoductos de plástico se instalan con un alambre de rastreo para ubicar la instalación. Si el alambre de rastreo se corta o daña, llame a SWG. Lo repararemos sin cargo.

 

TUBERÍAS DE ACERO Las tuberías de gas de acero, usadas por SWG tanto para la distribución de gas como para los sistemas de transmisión a alta presión, varían en tamaño desde 1/2" hasta 24" de diámetro y también son susceptibles a los daños. Las mellas y aberturas en el acero pueden afectar la integridad de la tubería. Por eso, deben tomarse medidas de precaución durante la excavación. Las tuberías de acero se protegen con un material de recubrimiento aprobado que ayuda a prevenir su deterioro y puede ser de varios colores. Si durante la excavación el recubrimiento se desprende o daña, comuníquese con SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones sin cargo. Llámenos antes de quitar cualquier recubrimiento de masilla de una tubería de acero activa o abandonada. Es posible que el recubrimiento contenga fibras de amianto reglamentario que pueden ser dañinas para sus empleados.

 

En general, las tuberías de gas tienen marcas de identificación específicas sobre ellas o sobre el recubrimiento. Debe tenerse precaución y sostener y proteger todos los gasoductos, según lo requiera la ley, cuando se expongan o crucen durante la excavación. Además, debe tenerse cuidado al exponer instalaciones existentes, ya que pueden o no, tener relleno a su alrededor, como se detalla más abajo. Si un gasoducto está dañado, llame a SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones necesarias. Cuando finalicen las excavaciones, los gasoductos deben ser rellenados según las normas de SWG, como se muestra en el dibujo más abajo. Las especificaciones de SWG para el material de relleno indican que este debe poder pasar a través de un tamiz de 3/8”, ser suave y estar relativamente libre de escombros.  Las excavaciones deben ser compactadas para cumplir con los requisitos de las autoridades locales. Durante el rellenado, es muy importante compactar el suelo bajo el gasoducto, a fin de sujetarlo apropiadamente. También es importante evitar compactar mecánicamente el suelo que está sobre el gasoducto para eliminar tensiones externas innecesarias. Deben tomarse medidas durante este proceso para proteger el gasoducto de cargas externas excesivas. Si se deben instalar otros servicios o subestructuras en la misma excavación del gasoducto, deben respetarse las distancias que se muestran en el dibujo.

Si en cualquier momento durante la excavación percibe olor a gas, llame a SWG y al 911.

*	NO intente controlar ni parar el flujo de gas natural ni de hacer reparaciones.
*	NO encienda, apague ni intente mover u operar equipos cerca del punto donde se rompió la línea o se produjo el escape.
*	NO entre en un área donde haya un escape de gas natural.
*	NO permita que otras personas entren en dicha área.
*	NO deje el lugar del incidente hasta que llegue la ayuda.
*	DESPEJE el área y evite que otras personas entren en ella.
*	ELIMINE las fuentes de combustión, como chispas o llamas, cerca de la atmósfera gaseosa.

Si desea más información sobre los tipos de tuberías de gas usados por SWG o sobre cómo identificar instalaciones de gas, o si tiene preguntas, llame a la oficina de SWG más cercana. En nuestra hoja de datos de seguridad de material (MSDS), puede encontrar más información sobre la seguridad con el gas natural. Esta se encuentra en www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .






Favor de hacer llegar al excavador correspondiente.

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8ca971cf-c92f-4689-a1dc-900919ac6f73/Eyebrows.png?t=1760976197> 	
 

  	Dear Readers,

Today, a single CEO's "no" to the Pentagon might redraw the boundaries of AI power forever. Dario Amodei rejected a $200 million defense contract rather than let Claude be used for mass surveillance or autonomous weapons, and what happens after the Friday deadline could set the rules for every AI company building for governments worldwide.

But that's far from the only seismic shift in today's issue: 

*	Isomorphic Labs just unveiled a drug design engine that more than doubles AlphaFold 3's accuracy

*	Epoch AI published a fascinating (and unsettling) analysis suggesting AI software efficiency may be improving up to 10× per year

*	Google dropped Nano Banana 2 to put pro-grade image generation in front of hundreds of millions of users for free; and

*	Burger King is now using an OpenAI-powered headset to police whether employees say "please" and "thank you" - because apparently the dystopia comes with a side of fries.

Grab your coffee and dig in.

  	

Superintelligence X GTC

Yesterday, NVIDIA released its latest quarterly results - and once again, they exceeded all analyst expectations.

With that in mind, I'm particularly curious how Jensen Huang will frame this momentum at this year's GTC keynote. Because GTC isn't just a product launch event. It's where NVIDIA defines the narrative for the next phase of AI.

Will we see deeper details on Vera Rubin and the post-Blackwell roadmap? More clarity on inference economics? Updates on NVL systems and sovereign AI factories? Or perhaps a broader vision for the next compute scaling frontier?

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a92dd46e-dd18-4b3b-88a0-14f08aca6e5a/Outline__7_.png?t=1772191341> 	
Historically, Jensen uses GTC to do three things: 

1.	Introduce the next architecture leap

2.	Expand NVIDIA's vertical integration across the AI stack 

3.	Reframe what the industry should focus on next. After another blowout quarter, the stakes feel even higher.

I'll be covering the keynote live from the ground this year, my first time attending GTC in person.

If you want to follow the keynote live from home, you can register via the following link: [NVIDIA GTC 2026 Keynote] <https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/ZquP6eSsYmvVQUhDUcN8lykdYSZJdistlUGjgHnzzCn9%2FpfYmgdwd4yHR%2FWv%0AxocvbXITcDS6KZ%2FetnrlaGq2piPLVjsfxmFXk7kuHAwyLEYZNLIDJqDTJ07p%0AjNBRWpkeDOprp0OpIG4hZ28ENKTgNgL6AR5DX29pgpn8%2FCbbGx8%3D%0A/de8c5f8c445f9c9a> 

All the best,

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/c82900b7-ebbf-4eb6-811f-86a9b3dac911/image.png?t=1756137355> 	
Kim Isenberg

  	
  	
 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7b665c8b-a655-4dd2-89d3-61bc24b2ab7e/Button.png?t=1760609218> 	
  	 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/f509b114-7eb9-43a3-8a8e-6bfb203a19bc/Eyebrows.png?t=1760708829> 	
 

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/0b791851-f06e-4e06-8699-094a246890d1/Outline__8_.png?t=1772191511> 	
 


🧬 IsoDDE Redefines AI Drug Discovery

Isomorphic Labs unveiled IsoDDE, an advanced AI drug design engine that more than doubles AlphaFold 3’s accuracy on the hardest protein–ligand benchmarks. It also beats physics-based methods like FEP in binding affinity prediction at a fraction of the cost and time.

IsoDDE delivers 2.3x stronger high-fidelity antibody–antigen predictions and can identify novel druggable pockets using only amino acid sequences. This signals a major step toward fully in-silico drug discovery at scale. (Note: Isomorphic Labs is an Alphabet-owned company closely linked to Google DeepMind, led by CEO Demis Hassabis).

Learn More <https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/ln3uuggsayU16dXWHcmtNgr%2FXy6lK0CF1GXFlFR07llqIgCclabIqylEsxlt%0AQT6qh4UgGq3HMgc6qvO08ODfIlwjO0SAcalbT%2FcWcEFSWWhlc0ZM2xkfr7SC%0AaZiDlvlKh%2FalUIILgu3s%2BSx5iHRQji0qisOFpB45jKeFeYYTZIY%3D%0A/2f9f8784b75a5ee9> 	
 

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eee95a11-7e50-4733-b7f4-e3c35420a438/Image_Aspect_Ratio__11_.png?t=1772191622> 	
 


🚀 Software progress reshapes AI timelines

Epoch AI argues that “AI software progress” mostly means cutting the training compute needed to reach the same capabilities. The best (though highly uncertain) evidence suggests efficiency could improve several-fold per year, with a personal best guess hovering around 10× per year (and a wide 2×–50× credible interval).

The twist: A lot of what we’ve been calling “algorithmic progress” may actually be better data curation, synthetic data, and scale-dependent innovations that only pay off when training larger models. This means past estimates might be measuring the wrong thing. subject: FW: Requirement for Engineer-Sealed Electrical Plans with Monument Sign Submittals
body:
Dear Sign Company Representatives,

 

Several questions have been raised regarding the recently communicated requirements for monument signs. We appreciate the feedback and are providing the following clarification to better define the scope and limitations of the requirement.

 

Engineer-sealed electrical plans are required only for the following:

 

*	Freeway monument signs

 

*	Monument signs over 35 feet in height

 

*	Monument signs located within a public right-of-way (ROW)

 

Please note that UL-listed signs do not require sealed drawings for the sign itself. However, site-specific electrical or structural components outside of the UL listing may still be subject to applicable code requirements.

 

If you have any questions regarding this clarification, please contact our office prior to submitting your application.

 

Thank you,

 

 



John Sheffer, PE, CBO │Deputy Director | Building Official 

Tel: (480) 644-5879

john.sheffer@mesaaz.gov  

55 N. Center St │ Mesa │ AZ │ 85201

Office Hours: M-Th 7am to 6pm | Closed Fridays & Holidays

 

 

From: John Sheffer 
Sent: Wednesday, February 25, 2026 9:24 AM
Cc: John Sheffer <John.Sheffer@MesaAZ.gov>
Subject: Requirement for Engineer-Sealed Electrical Plans with Monument Sign Submittals

 

Dear Sign Company Representatives,

 

The City is implementing a clarification to our monument sign submittal requirements. Effective immediately, all monument sign permit applications that include electrical components must include electrical plans sealed by a licensed professional engineer.

 

This requirement applies to all new monument signs and any modifications to existing monument signs that involve electrical work, including but not limited to illumination, digital displays, or other powered components. The engineer’s seal must be clearly affixed to the submitted electrical drawings in accordance with state licensing requirements.

 

Submittals that do not include properly sealed electrical plans will be deemed incomplete and will not proceed to plan review until the required documentation is provided.

 

This measure is intended to ensure compliance with applicable building and electrical codes and to promote public safety. We encourage you to review your internal processes to ensure that future submittals meet this requirement.

 

If you have any questions regarding this update, please contact our office prior to submitting your application.

 

Thank you for your cooperation.

 



John Sheffer, PE, CBO │Deputy Director | Building Official 

Tel: (480) 644-5879

john.sheffer@mesaaz.gov <mailto:john.sheffer@mesaaz.gov>   

55 N. Center St │ Mesa │ AZ │ 85201

Office Hours: M-Th 7am to 6pm | Closed Fridays & Holidays

subject: Town of Gilbert -  SIGN-2025-00283 Your Permit is Now Available
body:
Your approved permit is attached. Visit our OneStopShop <https://onestopshop.gilbertaz.gov/>  portal to download any approved plans. These can be viewed under the “attachments” section of your permit. Approved plans and permit must be printed and available at the time of your inspections. 

To print a copy of your permit, please use the printer icon in OneStopShop to print your permit. If you do not see the printer icon and your permit is in an "Issued" status, please contact us at EplanBuilding@gilbertaz.gov. 

A one-time registration is required. If you have not already registered, please use this link <https://onestopshop.gilbertaz.gov/>  to do so. Please allow one business day following your registration to gain full access to the OneStopShop portal. 

You will also be able to request inspections as well as monitor inspection results. The OneStopShop is also available for online payments and to apply for future permits. 

For any questions, please call our Development Services team (480) 503-6700, Mon-Thurs 7am-6pm. Offices are closed Fridays and Holidays. 

Thank you, 

Town of Gilbert
Development Services
Ph: 480-503-6700

*We are transitioning online applications from our current ePlan Review to OneStopShop. OneStopShop online applications are currently limited to select permit types: Commercial and Residential Trade permits, Swimming pools, Engineering Utility Permits, Deferred Submittals and Plan Changes. All others must be applied for through our ePlan Review <http://general.gilbertaz.gov/eforms/eplan/BLDGSubmits/ePlanAppConst.cfm>  process.

subject: Town of Gilbert SIGN-2025-00283 Sign permit issued
body:
Dear Customer, 

Thank you for obtaining your permit for your signage here in Gilbert. Please be aware you will need to schedule and complete all applicable inspections relating to this permit. Approved plans must be on-site at the time of your inspection. Please login to our OneStopShop <https://onestopshop.gilbertaz.gov/>  to print your approved plans, pay fees and schedule all inspections. Approved plans can be viewed/printed under the “attachments” section of your permit. 

At this time your scheduled inspection may be eligible for either an onsite or virtual inspection*. The area inspector will contact you if your inspection is eligible to be conducted virtually, otherwise your onsite inspection will be completed as scheduled.

Approved plans and permit must be printed and available at the time of your inspection(s).

For any questions, please call our Development Services team (480) 503-6700, Mon-Thurs 7am-6pm. Offices are closed Fridays and Holidays.

Thank you, 
Town of Gilbert
Development Services
Ph: 480-503-6700 

*For Virtual Inspections, you will need to have the following items:
1.) Measuring tape
2.) Copy of permit application and plans indicating proper distancing and location of sign 
3.) Phone availability of either Facetime, Zoom, Teams or another software program that will allow face to face interaction with the inspector.

subject: Re: B25-1777 – First Credit Union – Signage Allowance Inquiry (South Elevation) (02/25/26)
body:
Hi Steve,

The total sign area allowed per the sign regulations (Article 7, Section 2 of the Zoning Ordinance) shall not exceed 150 square feet. Although the approved signage under B25-0177 lies at approximately 91.5 square feet in total sign coverage, the south-facing elevation does project toward residential properties adjacent to the site. 

As stated further on in the sign regulations, signs identifying a business in a non-residential zoning district are not permitted on the building façade adjacent to a shared zoning district boundary with a residential zoning district. 

Respectfully, 

Nathan Warren	​​​​

subject: Requirement for Engineer-Sealed Electrical Plans with Monument Sign Submittals
body:
Dear Sign Company Representatives,

 

The City is implementing a clarification to our monument sign submittal requirements. Effective immediately, all monument sign permit applications that include electrical components must include electrical plans sealed by a licensed professional engineer.

 

This requirement applies to all new monument signs and any modifications to existing monument signs that involve electrical work, including but not limited to illumination, digital displays, or other powered components. The engineer’s seal must be clearly affixed to the submitted electrical drawings in accordance with state licensing requirements.

 

Submittals that do not include properly sealed electrical plans will be deemed incomplete and will not proceed to plan review until the required documentation is provided.

 

This measure is intended to ensure compliance with applicable building and electrical codes and to promote public safety. We encourage you to review your internal processes to ensure that future submittals meet this requirement.

 

If you have any questions regarding this update, please contact our office prior to submitting your application.

 

Thank you for your cooperation.

 



John Sheffer, PE, CBO │Deputy Director | Building Official

?         Height, width, and length of all letters and logos

Hi Taryn,

I wanted to follow up regarding PMT26-01022 – Sherwin-Williams (1202 University Dr.) and your correction comment under §11-43-2B1.a.i or ii.

We recently spoke with a Planner of the Day, who reviewed the proposed sign plans and recognized that the signs are pan-channel letters mounted on a backer panel, not cabinet signs.

To clarify the construction method, we are providing the attached channel letter installation cut sheet, which demonstrates how the pan-channel letters are mounted and wired, including attachment and structural details. subject: INVOICE | BLDC-26-0049
body:
Good morning.

Your permit application has been reviewed and approved by our plan reviewer(s).

Please refer to the invoice number for payment details. Once payment is received, your permit status will be updated to Issued.

Hi Jeremiah,

 

Thank you — I appreciate that. A tour would be helpful once we have a clearer direction.

 

Gilbert’s sign code can be rather restrictive, particularly if the property is zoned residential or Business Park. For example, in residential districts, high-mounted wall signage is generally not permitted unless it falls within a defined architectural sign band and meets specific dimensional criteria. Illumination can also be limited depending on adjacency. Because of this, we may have very limited options — possibly none — depending on the zoning designation.

 

Before proceeding with a site visit, survey, or proposal development, I’d like to confirm the zoning through the parcel number and have a preliminary discussion with the city to make sure we clearly understand what is permitted.

 

Once we confirm that framework, I’ll follow up and we can coordinate next steps, including a visit if appropriate.

 

Thanks again — I’ll be in touch soon.

Hi Casey,

Thank you for the additional information — that’s very helpful.


If the sign is currently right at 25’ from the Miller Road property line, and there is the ability to shift it back a few additional feet, if necessary, that could be a viable resolution. However, since the County’s concern relates specifically to the future ROW line, we will need formal documentation to confirm compliance.


The most practical next step would be to perform a Boundary / Spot Survey to:

*	Verify the exact property line location
*	Dimension the sign pole to that property line
*	Confirm whether the sign is fully outside the future ROW
*	Identify any easements that may affect placement


This would provide a stamped exhibit we can submit to the County to demonstrate compliance and potentially avoid pursuing a ROW permit or relocating power.


Please let us know if you would like to move forward with this survey route to formally verify the setback and address the County’s requirements.


Once we have that documentation, we can confidently determine whether the existing location (or a minor adjustment) resolves the issue.

Hi Michelle,




Absolutely — here’s a simplified breakdown of what Mesa is asking for based on the correction notice 

and the referenced code section:




What the City Is Requiring

Mesa is reviewing this as an attached permanent sign, and it must comply with §11-43-2B1.a.i or ii. That means the sign must be either:

Option 1 – Individual Letters

*         Pan channel (or similar durable) letters

*         No visible attachment devices

*         No standard rectangular cabinet

OR

Option 2 – Architecturally Designed Cabinet

*         Cabinet must be irregular and freeform in shape

*         Not a standard box-style cabinet

*         Mounting hardware cannot be visible

________________________________

What This Likely Means for This Submittal

The current design appears to be a rectangular aluminum cabinet, which does not meet Mesa’s design standards for attached signs.

Mesa is essentially asking that the sign either:

*         Be revised to individual channel letters, or

*         Be redesigned as an architecturally integrated, non-rectangular cabinet, or

*         Pursue a Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP) if the standard cannot be met.


If helpful, I would be happy to hop on a conference call with Taryn Martinez (480-644-5459) to clarify exactly what they are looking for and confirm the most efficient path forward. A brief discussion can often prevent an unnecessary resubmittal cycle and provide clear direction.

Hi Michelle,



Absolutely — here’s a simplified breakdown of what Mesa is asking for based on the correction notice 

and the referenced code section:



What the City Is Requiring

Mesa is reviewing this as an attached permanent sign, and it must comply with §11-43-2B1.a.i or ii. That means the sign must be either:

Option 1 – Individual Letters

*         Pan channel (or similar durable) letters

*         No visible attachment devices

*         No standard rectangular cabinet

OR

Option 2 – Architecturally Designed Cabinet

*         Cabinet must be irregular and freeform in shape

*         Not a standard box-style cabinet

*         Mounting hardware cannot be visible

________________________________

What This Likely Means for This Submittal

The current design appears to be a rectangular aluminum cabinet, which does not meet Mesa’s design standards for attached signs.

Mesa is essentially asking that the sign either:

*         Be revised to individual channel letters, or

*         Be redesigned as an architecturally integrated, non-rectangular cabinet, or

*         Pursue a Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP) if the standard cannot be met.


If helpful, I would be happy to hop on a conference call with Taryn Martinez (480-644-5459) to clarify exactly what they are looking for and confirm the most efficient path forward. A brief discussion can often prevent an unnecessary resubmittal cycle and provide clear direction.

We just received the City of Mesa’s review comments for Sherwin Williams #701582 (see email and corrections attached).


The correction references Mesa City Code §11-43-2(B)(1)(a)(i) or (ii), which addresses the allowable wall sign area calculation. The City is asking that the proposed sign be revised and/or clearly documented to demonstrate compliance with one of those provisions.


I’ve attached the City’s correction report and the Mesa sign code for reference. Once the revised plans are ready, they can be resubmitted to keep the permit moving forward.

Good morning,  

Thank you for taking my call! I wanted to reach out to you regarding some upcoming warranty service work we have in your area. We have a work order for a Floor & Decor in Scottsdale, AZ.

subject: BLDC-26-0049 - Structural design and calculations required
body:
Hi Steve,

I wanted to follow up regarding the sign submittal on BLDC-26-0049. I received clarification from my supervisors after our conversation on the “per ASA requirements” note. While we understand that reference may have been used on prior projects, we are not able to approve the sign based on that note alone. 

The current plans do not include enough structural information to verify compliance (e.g., sign structure member sizing/materials, anchorage/base-plate details, foundation/footing design, and applicable design criteria). To proceed, please submit structural plans and supporting calculations for the sign structure and foundation/anchorage. Documents must be prepared by a design professional, as applicable, and should clearly indicate the design criteria used (wind, exposure, etc.) along with all connection and footing details.

 

 

 <https://www.buckeyeaz.gov/>

From: Steve Skye <steve@christysigns.com>
Sent: Wednesday, February 11, 2026 8:45:26 AM
To: Rocky Marsh <rocky@christysigns.com>
Subject: Burros & Fries – CSP / Sign Code Conflict Update (02/11/26) 
 

Hi Rocky,



I wanted to discuss with you the recent correspondence with Dana Stevens, Planning Specialist for the Town of Gilbert regarding the Burros & Fries sign permit application.



Planning has clarified their position that the Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP) does not authorize signage beyond what the Gilbert sign code allows. In short, they are requiring the wall signs to meet base code limits, even though the CSP exhibits depict larger approved sign areas.  

 

This creates a procedural conflict between:

*	The stamped CSP exhibits (approved December 17, 2025), and
*	Planning’s current interpretation that the CSP does not override code allowances.


At this point, we have two possible paths:

1.	Obtain formal clarification from Planning confirming whether the CSP was intended to modify sign allowances, or
2.	Revise the CPS removing the generic language concerning adhering to the Gilbert sign code.


I have placed calls to the Town of Gilbert Planning Department to obtain additional clarity on how CSP approvals are intended to function relative to the sign ordinance. I am waiting for a return call so we can determine the correct course before making design adjustments.


I’ll update you as soon as I receive further guidance.


Regards,

 

Steve Skye

subject: city of Buckeye Permit has been issued - BLDC-26-0029
body:
Your permit is now in Issued status, and the approved plans and documents are available online through the Citizen Self-Service (CSS) Portal. Inspections can be scheduled online through the portal. Please follow the instructions below to access, print your permit, and download approved plans.

 

How to Print a Permit 

1.	Log in to the CSS Portal: City of Buckeye <https://egselfservice.buckeyeaz.gov/energov_prod/selfservice#/home>  

	*	Note: Registration is required to access records. If you do not have an account, you must create one before proceeding.

2.	Locate Your Permit: 

	*	Click on the “Dashboard” tab.
	*	Find your permits under “My Permits”, or use the search bar to locate them.

Hi Scott,




We’ve received the correction comments from the Town of Queen Creek for the First Watch – Harvest Station sign permit.


The Planning review is complete, and the project is currently on hold pending revisions. I’ve attached the following for reference:

*	Town of Queen Creek Corrections Report
*	Harvest Station Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP)
*	Current First Watch sign drawings and elevations


In summary, the Town is requiring revisions in two key areas:

1.	Wall Sign / Raceway Design
	The proposed wall signs do not currently meet the CSP requirement for architecturally integrated raceways. The CSP requires individual channel letters integrated into a designed signage wireway or sign band that is complementary to the building architecture, rather than a standard exposed raceway. The sign details and elevations will need to be revised accordingly.
2.	Sign Area Calculations
	The submittal must clearly document building frontage dimensions and provide sign area calculations per the CSP (1.5 SF per linear foot, max 250 SF per building). These calculations need to be shown directly on the plans.


Once the sign design and calculations are updated, we can prepare a full resubmittal package and response letter addressing each comment.  Let me know if able to be of any additional assistance.

subject: Scottsdale Planning and Development - Phishing Scam Alert
sender_name: City of Scottsdale Planning and Development
body:
View In Browser <https://newsletters.scottsdaleaz.gov/trk/clickp?ref=zvbdm4r20_2-32csrvn-0-2a7b_0x314d67x01213:::VIBPB:::&a3=570&a2=permits%40CHRISTYSIGNS.COM&a0=1213&a4=permits%40christysigns.com&a1=%26AMP%3B%3B:::VIBPE:::> 

 <https://newsletters.scottsdaleaz.gov/trk/click?ref=zvbdm4r20_2-32csrvn-0-2a7b_0x32812x01213> 	 

Dear Scottsdale Planning and Development Services Customer:
 

We are aware of an email phishing scam in which the sender is posing as our department. While the email messages vary in content, the request is the same: respond to the email for instructions on wiring funds.
 

The messages may appear authentic as they reference recent planning and development cases and board and commission decisions. However, there are key indicators of it being a scam.

1.	The email address comes from planning-scottsdaleaz.gov @usa.com. Legitimate city communications will always come from an email address ending in "@scottsdaleaz.gov." While "scottsdaleaz.gov" may be within the fraudulent email address, it has a "@usa.com" suffix which indicates it is not an official city of Scottsdale email.
	 
2.	The email requires you to reply for a payment link and instructions. Fee payments will always be collected through our secure website portal or in person at the One Stop Shop. Visit our Planning and Development Services webpage for the accurate city of Scottsdale portal links and log in to your account to see fees that are due. We never request customers to "wire funds."

Please remember that we launched a new planning and permitting portal, Scottsdale SPUR, on Jan. 6, 2026. Projects initiated before this date will continue to be managed within the eServices portal, unless you are notified otherwise. Projects initiated after this date will be managed in Scottsdale SPUR.
 

If you receive a message you believe to be a phishing scam, please forward it to Planning and Development Services’ systems analyst Angel Gonzalez at AGonzalez@ScottsdaleAZ.gov <https://newsletters.scottsdaleaz.gov/trk/click?ref=zvbdm4r20_2-32csrvn-0-2a7b_0x314d68x01213> .
 

Customers are encouraged to call our department at 480-312-3111, or the planner assigned to your case, for information related to your project.
 

Please do not reply to this message as it was sent from a mailbox that is not monitored.

You may also visit us at ScottsdaleAZ.gov <https://newsletters.scottsdaleaz.gov/trk/click?ref=zvbdm4r20_2-32csrvn-0-2a7b_0x32865x01213> . This email was sent to &EMAIL;.

Unsubscribe or manage your email subscriptions <https://newsletters.scottsdaleaz.gov/trk/clickp?ref=zvbdm4r20_2-32csrvn-0-2a7b_0x31a68x01213&t=&EMAIL;> .

subject: INSTALLATION QUOTE REQUEST--ROSS DRESS FOR LESS--#2832 CHANDLER, AZ
body:
Hi Scott & Steve—

 

I’m sending another installation quote request for the Ross Dress For Less #2832 at Desert Palms/ Sun Village in Chandler, AZ.  I believe you’re doing a lot of the work here as well?  This store opens October 9, 2026.

 

PERMITTING--I’ve had multiple discussions with Mr. Joseph Sauer, the Site Development Director, at the City of Chandler.  Very nice man.  Though we were originally going to need an MSP Amendment for this location, he is allowing us to calculate the SF of the channel letters using multiple boxes, which brings us to the exact allowance of 252.0 SF (2SF/1LF of frontage).  He has already previewed the attached drawings, and will expedite permit approval within a day or two of submittal.  That said, he did have some specific permitting “rules” and directions he wants us to follow that I will forward separately.  

 

I saw in our renderings from the Landlord (Bob Rusing & Dave Schwartz) that you fabricated the monument signs.  Can you fabricate the ROPT copy for ROSS if I send you the vector files?  Bob said it’s fine for the panels to be removed for the time it will take to do the work.  

 

Any chance you could send me your bid by TOMORROW?  😊  

 

I will send your Permit PO along with LL-approved artwork for Steve to begin the permitting process separately, along with directions from Mr. Sauer.  If there is anything else needed for permitting, please let me know.  

 

Thank you!

Amy

Hello Dane, During the pool service visit on January 28th, 2026, Caleb carefully maintained your pool to ensure it stays in great condition. The pool was thoroughly skimmed, and chemical levels were tested. One chlorine tab was added to maintain the balance. Caleb noted that the pool's water chemistry is mostly within the ideal ranges for the cooler months. The free and total chlorine levels were at 1 ppm, and the pH was measured at 7.2, both within the ideal range. Total alkalinity was at a healthy 100 ppm.
